nodes.label: Varnish 7.5 edge-cache service
nodes.rationale: Not a standalone stack — an overlay in front of an already-running app service; Varnish does not terminate TLS, so a terminator must sit in front of it.

nodes.label: Adoption is a two-sided change
nodes.rationale: Starting the container alone adds a hop for no gain: the app must set EDGE_CACHE_MODE, purge endpoint and token and schedule edge-cache:purge. Enable the app side first, confirm Surrogate-Control, then put the container in front — that ordering avoids a stale-content window.

nodes.label: default_ttl=0 / default_grace=0 belt-and-braces
nodes.rationale: Even if vcl_backend_response were bypassed an untagged response gets zero TTL rather than Varnish's stock 120s, so three independent layers must fail before an untagged response is cached.

nodes.label: EDGE_CACHE_PURGE_TOKEN shared secret
nodes.rationale: A mismatch makes every invalidation fail with 403 and the site silently serves stale content — which is why security:readiness treats a configured endpoint without a token as a hard failure, not a warning.

nodes.label: Malloc storage sizing vs ban lurker
nodes.rationale: Bans are evaluated against every object until the lurker collects them, so an oversized cache makes invalidation slower, not merely memory-hungrier; size to hot content, not the total corpus.

nodes.label: Frozen open-redirect guard
nodes.rationale: Redirect targets must be a relative same-origin path or an absolute URL to one of the tenant's verified hosts; unsafe/cross-host/protocol-relative/CRLF/loop/over-long-chain targets rejected.

nodes.label: Sync Storage module (API surface)
nodes.rationale: Admin bearer-session views (conflicts/nodes/object-queue) distinct from the machine-to-machine HMAC push/pull/status/objects endpoints.

nodes.label: HMAC-authenticated sync (push/pull/status/objects)
nodes.rationale: syncHmac + tenantHeader security with SyncNodeId/Timestamp/Signature; push is idempotent per batchId, pull is checkpoint-based; a deactivated node is rejected 403 immediately.

nodes.label: Tenant Domain module (hostname mappings)
nodes.rationale: Manual-first domain verification and single-primary selection; duplicate hostname always returns a generic conflict that never reveals cross-tenant ownership.

nodes.label: Theming module (draft/publish/rollback)
nodes.rationale: Data-only theme config validated against a build-time theme descriptor (CSS-injection spine); publish creates immutable versions; token values validated against strict CSS grammars.

nodes.label: Visitor Analytics module (API surface)
nodes.rationale: Public anonymous fire-and-forget beacon (always 202, never leaks tenant existence) plus permission-gated dashboards; raw detail hidden unless the caller holds raw_detail.read.

nodes.label: Workflow Approval module (API surface)
nodes.rationale: Versioned workflow definitions (draft/active/retired), a consolidated approval inbox, quorum-gated task decisions, delegations, and administrative force/reassign recovery; self-approval denied.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL Migration Runner
nodes.rationale: Bun.SQL-based runner reading sql/ ordered by filename; skips recorded migrations, stores SHA-256 per applied file, never prints DATABASE_URL in errors.

nodes.label: Step 0 — Take AND Verify a Backup
nodes.rationale: Migrations are forward-only (no down), so restore is the only rollback path; a dump never restore-tested is just a file, not a rollback path. The verify-only drill also proves FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY survives the round-trip — lost tenant isolation after a restore is a silent failure.
nodes.norm_label: step 0 — take and verify a backup

nodes.label: Advisory Lock + lock_timeout/statement_timeout
nodes.rationale: lock_timeout=5s stops one DDL waiting on ACCESS EXCLUSIVE from queueing every request behind it (the usual way a quick ALTER TABLE takes the site down); statement_timeout=15min bounds a runaway backfill. A migration needing longer says so with SET LOCAL inside its own file, where the reviewer looks.

nodes.label: Applied-Migration Checksum Immutability
nodes.rationale: If an already-applied migration changes, the runner stops and demands a new migration instead of silently re-running or ignoring the drift.

nodes.label: Forward-Only Migrations
nodes.rationale: There is no down migration; the only real rollback is a restore from a verified backup.

nodes.label: Bun.SQL Pool Configuration
nodes.rationale: Session GUCs such as statement_timeout are applied via the `connection` option, not `onconnect` — onconnect is typed (err)=>void and gives no client to run SQL, despite a misleading JSDoc example in bun-types.

nodes.label: Work-Class Concurrency Gate
nodes.rationale: Five fixed, non-env-tunable limits kept far below DATABASE_POOL_MAX so the Bun.SQL pool keeps headroom; ordering follows priority (critical_transaction largest, maintenance serialised at 1 because it is not an interactive HTTP concern).

nodes.label: Bounded Work-Class Queue
nodes.rationale: Closes the cascading-timeout-chain risk: an unbounded queue makes every caller wait the full timeoutMs before failing. WorkClassQueueFullError rejects immediately (never waits) and is a distinct type from WorkClassTimeoutError so callers map it type-safely to 503 DATABASE_BUSY + Retry-After.

nodes.label: Database Circuit Breaker
nodes.rationale: A pure function of an injected `now` (no hidden Date.now()) so it is unit-testable without real time; one module-level singleton shared application-wide so failures across requests/tenants produce a single fail-fast decision.

nodes.label: withTenant as the Single Integration Point
nodes.rationale: Every endpoint already calls withTenant, so gate+breaker protection applies automatically without touching every route.
nodes.norm_label: withtenant as the single integration point

nodes.label: SQLSTATE Class 22/23 Breaker Exemptions
nodes.rationale: FK/unique/check violations (class 23) and data exceptions (class 22, e.g. a non-UUID compared to a uuid column) are caller-input errors, not infra failures — counting them would let a handful of malformed requests open an application-wide breaker. IdempotencyRaceLostError is exempt for the same reason.

nodes.label: GET /api/v1/database/pool/health
nodes.rationale: Reports aggregates only (counts/booleans), never tenant data or query contents; the DB probe is a bare SELECT 1 via getDatabaseClient (not withTenant, since the endpoint is not tenant-scoped) wrapped in try/catch so a DB outage cannot crash the health check itself.

nodes.label: PgBouncer Transaction Mode
nodes.rationale: Optional and Compose-profile-gated; DATABASE_PGBOUNCER=true forces prepare:false because prepared statements break when each statement may land on a different backend. Application code is already safe because withTenant uses SET LOCAL, whose scope is one transaction.

nodes.label: Deployment-Aware Connection Capacity
nodes.rationale: Sections 1-7 protect ONE process; the approved PostgreSQL/PgBouncer budget applies to the whole fleet. capacity-config.ts is real at runtime; the CLI wrapper database:capacity:check is not.

nodes.label: database.pool.saturated Event
nodes.rationale: No pub/sub dispatcher exists; the concrete producer is a structured log line, so the AsyncAPI entry is a documented contract only.

nodes.label: One Coolify App per Environment
nodes.rationale: ADR-0083: this repo deploys one environment because it is a template validated by the CI gate chain plus the Postgres integration suite, not a business. Environments sharing one Coolify app share env vars — exactly how a second environment accidentally writes to production data.

nodes.label: Verify Against the Control-Plane, Not curl
nodes.rationale: On 11 Aug 2026 awcms.ahlikoding.com answered 200 while its production application row and database did not exist — a staging Varnish container's two-host Traefik rule served the production domain. A 200 proves a container answers, not that production is alive; proof lives in Coolify's applications/standalone_postgresqls tables.
nodes.norm_label: verify against the control-plane, not curl

nodes.label: Pattern 1 — Build from the GitHub Repo
nodes.norm_label: pattern 1 — build from the github repo

nodes.label: Pattern 2 — Pull the Image from a Registry
nodes.rationale: Immutable image per release, one build used everywhere, keeps the Coolify build server light; release.yml already pushes to ghcr.io/ahliweb/awcms.
nodes.norm_label: pattern 2 — pull the image from a registry

nodes.label: Image Tags Carry No v Prefix
nodes.rationale: release.yml strips it (VERSION=${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}), so git tag v7.0.1 produces :7.0.1; :v7.0.1 does not exist and fails to pull. Pin an explicit version in Coolify, not :latest.
nodes.norm_label: image tags carry no v prefix

nodes.label: Single VPS / Same Docker Host Topology
nodes.rationale: The database needs no public port when only the app on the same Docker network reaches it. A single VPS is a single point of failure — a deliberate MVP/small-production trade-off, not an HA recommendation.
nodes.norm_label: single vps / same docker host topology

nodes.label: Multi-Application-on-One-VPS Topology
nodes.rationale: Per application: own domain, own secrets (never reuse AUTH_IP_HASH_SECRET/sync HMAC/MFA key), own database or at minimum own schema+role, own backup schedule, internal hostnames only.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL Options for Multiple Applications
nodes.rationale: One cluster many databases (efficient, larger blast radius) vs one container per app (best isolation, resource-hungry) vs external/managed (HA/compliance, network + cost). All three keep least-privilege runtime role, FORCE RLS, and migrations as a separate privileged step.

nodes.label: One-Shot Migration Before First Deploy
nodes.rationale: Dockerfile.production does not run migrations — its runtime role awcms_app has no DDL/GRANT rights. Each application/database gets its own one-shot migration; never run one app's migration against another's database.

nodes.label: Backup Verified Before Every db:migrate
nodes.rationale: ADR-0083 records a restore-verified backup as the replacement for the missing pre-production rehearsal — a mitigation, not an equivalent. The one-shot container must use a postgres image matching the server version; an older pg_dump refuses a newer server.

nodes.label: Coolify Health Check Path
nodes.rationale: GET /api/v1/health proves the container answering that domain is healthy — not WHICH container answers; for that, read the Coolify control-plane tables.

nodes.label: Scheduled Dispatchers as One-Shot Containers
nodes.rationale: Dockerfile.production is runtime-only and ships no scripts/, so docker exec bun run email:dispatch fails with Module not found while looking scheduled. Run a one-shot container from a checkout at the DEPLOYED release tag, sharing the DB container's netns.

nodes.label: Deploy Rollback and Migration Caution
nodes.rationale: An image rollback does not undo applied schema migrations — the old app can end up on an incompatible new schema. Test expand-first compatibility and keep a restorable backup as the schema rollback path.

nodes.label: Three Deployment Profiles
nodes.rationale: ModuleDeploymentProfile is development|production|offline-lan. staging was REMOVED from the vocabulary (ADR-0083), not merely unused: a profile nobody has ever drilled is a claim, not a capability, yet it clings to every module descriptor, doc table, and APP_ENV branch.

nodes.label: Two-Role Database Model (RLS Enforcement)
nodes.rationale: ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY alone is not enough: Postgres bypasses RLS for the table owner unless FORCE, and unconditionally for SUPERUSER/BYPASSRLS. A privileged migration role is therefore separated from the least-privilege runtime role awcms_app, with a fail-closed default GUC (zero UUID matches no tenant).

nodes.label: Optional awcms_worker / awcms_setup Roles
nodes.rationale: Defense-in-depth roles from sql/022 with GRANTs only for the write paths their code uses; both fall back to DATABASE_URL if unset, so the two-role model stays the mandatory minimum.

nodes.label: TLS / Trust Boundaries per Topology
nodes.rationale: The app never terminates TLS. app's 4321 is still bound to 0.0.0.0 by default, so a client can bypass the reverse proxy entirely — the firewall mitigation is mandatory, because AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE=true assumes the browser really speaks HTTPS.

nodes.label: Container Hardening Standard
nodes.rationale: db/pgbouncer publish no host ports; every service runs cap_drop ALL + no-new-privileges + healthcheck + resource limits. APP_UID/APP_GID export is mandatory or the container writes root-owned node_modules/dist into the bind mount and blocks host-side builds.

nodes.label: bun run config:validate
nodes.rationale: Required non-empty: APP_ENV, APP_URL, DATABASE_URL — bound to RULES in scripts/validate-env.ts by a test, so changing one without the other reddens the gate. APP_TIMEZONE and AUTH_JWT_SECRET were removed because no code reads them. Never prints secret values.

nodes.label: Job Registry (ModuleDescriptor.jobs)
nodes.rationale: The descriptor is the source of truth, not this document: a previous copied list aged into three ERP commands that never existed while the ten real jobs went unmentioned. modules:jobs:check and db:work-class:check enforce it; edge-cache:purge is the one recorded structural exception because there is no edge_cache module to hang a descriptor on.

nodes.label: runJob — Advisory Lock per Job Name
nodes.rationale: pg_try_advisory_lock on a reserved connection, bounded batching with maxPasses, error classification, redaction via sanitizeErrorForLog, cooperative SIGTERM cancellation with a grace period so the next tick does not claim a lock still held mid-shutdown.
nodes.norm_label: runjob — advisory lock per job name

nodes.label: Per-Row Claim-Lease Concurrency Model
nodes.rationale: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED makes overlapping invocations safe and actually ALLOWS parallel workers — a different guarantee from the advisory lock. A previous doc version claimed all seven dispatchers used runJob, misleading the reader in the dangerous direction.

nodes.label: Local Backup Mandatory on All Non-Dev Profiles
nodes.rationale: A restore-verified backup is a PREREQUISITE for migration, not a chore beside it. Encryption at rest and an HMAC-signed manifest are not implemented — the scripts refuse to run when those key vars are set so nobody believes a plain dump is encrypted.
nodes.norm_label: local backup mandatory on all non-dev profiles

nodes.label: Offline-First Mandatory for Core ERP Operations
nodes.rationale: Daily transactions, inventory, HR attendance and manufacturing must run without internet; only inherently online features may be deferred, and they must go through the outbox rather than synchronous calls on the critical transaction path.
nodes.norm_label: offline-first mandatory for core erp operations

nodes.label: Derived-Repo Pathway Revoked (ADR-0034)
nodes.rationale: The AWCMS family is now a set of used-directly templates with no derivative repo; domain modules are developed directly in the template. These pilot documents are kept only as historical record.

nodes.label: Pilot Candidate Matrix
nodes.rationale: Five candidates scored on business need, security/privacy risk (lower better), data complexity, platform-validation value, implementation readiness and relevance; readiness is the sharpest differentiator.

nodes.label: AWPOS as First Derived Pilot
nodes.rationale: Lowest privacy risk of the five, repo/docs/38 issues/milestones already exist, and AWPOS is where this base's own standard came from — so validating AWPOS proves the base is genuinely general-purpose. 18 of its 38 issues are already done generically by AWCMS, leaving 20 domain-specific ones.

nodes.label: Purchase Requisition Increment-1 Scope
nodes.rationale: A deliberately neutral, minimal domain: draft→submit→approve/reject through the AWCMS workflow, plus events/audit/idempotency/tests — WITHOUT purchase order, receiving, invoice, accounting posting, tax, inventory or payment.

nodes.label: VENDOR Base Consumption Model
nodes.rationale: Copy the base tree, fill application-registry.ts as the only edited base file, pin the vendored version in the family manifest; upgrade = re-vendor. Guardrail ADR-0013: src/modules/index.ts and base module.ts files are never touched.

nodes.label: Three Composition Gates
nodes.rationale: modules:compose:check, modules:composition:inventory:check and extension:check — pure, no I/O, part of bun run check.

nodes.label: Plan Reality-Checks Against the Code
nodes.rationale: The extension.manifest.json gate does not exist; production:preflight has no script; AUTH_JWT_SECRET is not used by the base (the docs were wrong) — only APP_ENV/APP_URL/DATABASE_URL are required.

nodes.label: Verified Base Seam Map
nodes.rationale: Signatures quoted from real base code for authorizeInTransaction, evaluateAccess, withTenant, the workflow decision trio, appendDomainEvent, recordAuditEvent, idempotency helpers, api-response and keyset pagination — reused as-is, never reimplemented.

nodes.label: High-Risk Mutation Route Chain
nodes.rationale: Order matters: fetch the task early so requestedByTenantUserId is available for the self-approval check, guard BEFORE the idempotency replay lookup, and build the response before saveIdempotencyRecord.

nodes.label: submit Is Not a Valid AccessAction
nodes.rationale: Seeding purchase_requisition.requisition.submit would create an action that never passes the guard — a silent default-deny. Either add submit to the union as a non-high-risk action via a generic base PR, or use activityCode requisition_submission + action create.
nodes.norm_label: submit is not a valid accessaction

nodes.label: PR-Specific Approve/Reject Endpoint
nodes.rationale: The generic workflow endpoint guards only WORKFLOW permissions, so the SoD rule create-vs-approve would never fire there. A PR-owned endpoint plus looking up requestedByTenantUserId before the guard is what makes SoD and self-approval actually bite.

nodes.label: Requester ≠ Approver SoD Rule
nodes.rationale: sodRules flow automatically into enforcement via collectSoDRuleDescriptors(listModules()); no per-route wiring. reject is non-high-risk so the action-time SoD gate deliberately does not fire on it.

nodes.label: Keyset Cursor Microsecond Precision Pitfall
nodes.rationale: timestamptz is microseconds, JS Date only milliseconds — a cursor built from a Date skips rows inside the same millisecond. Carry created_at_cursor as full-precision TEXT from the SELECT.

nodes.label: migrationNamespace Is Purely Declarative
nodes.rationale: The composition gate compares the declared 900–999 range against the base constant 1–899; it never reads sql/*.sql. The physical file numbers are only a runner convention.

nodes.label: Mandatory Tenant-Scoped Schema Rules
nodes.rationale: Composite (tenant_id, xxx_id) FKs are required because the referential-integrity check runs as OWNER and bypasses RLS — a single-column FK can point across tenants even under FORCE. ENABLE then FORCE, tenant-prefixed indexes, and no GRANT needed thanks to sql/019's blanket grant.

nodes.label: Permission Seed Migration Is Mandatory
nodes.rationale: awcms_permissions is a GLOBAL catalogue with no tenant_id and no RLS; the module.ts descriptor is only synced lazily, so without the seed migration the bootstrap owner role is default-denied until the next sync.

nodes.label: Nine-Step Derived Application Flow
nodes.rationale: PRD/SRS → scaffold module → migration+RLS → seed RBAC/ABAC → endpoints+OpenAPI/events+AsyncAPI → UI → audit/observability → layered tests+security review → deployment. Each step maps to a real skill; do not guess the pattern.

nodes.label: Reusable Base vs Domain-Specific Extension
nodes.rationale: Keep the left column as it is, add the right column following established patterns — do not rewrite your own RLS/ABAC/audit/idempotency, the base already provides them.

nodes.label: application-registry.ts Composition Seam
nodes.rationale: Since Issue #178 a derived app replaces one `undefined` instead of editing src/modules/index.ts; composeModuleRegistry validates duplicate keys, base-key overrides, the dependency DAG, capability bindings, migration namespaces, profiles, navigation and jobs before a build counts as legitimate.

nodes.label: BusinessScopeHierarchyPort Resolver Contract
nodes.rationale: The base ships a no-op resolver returning resolved:false for every scope type, so scope-gated high-risk actions deny by default (fail-closed by design). A real resolver must enforce tenant isolation, bounded depth with cycle detection, and must not conflate resolved:false with 'no ancestors'.

nodes.label: Practical Security & Compliance Checklist
nodes.rationale: Security tests must force RLS/ABAC to FAIL to prove the gate really blocks, not merely that the happy path passes.

nodes.label: Derived CI Responsibilities
nodes.rationale: listModules() is deliberately pure data and does not validate at load time, so skipping modules:compose:check can boot an app with a duplicate-key registry that poisons permission/navigation seeding. An omitted migrationNamespace SKIPS the overlap check entirely, letting derived numbering collide silently.

nodes.label: Module Maturity: experimental → active
nodes.rationale: Descriptive metadata other contributors read to judge maturity, not a runtime gate.

nodes.label: Five Illustrative Derived Applications
nodes.rationale: AWPOS, Satu Sehat Kobar, Health Facility QMS, Smart School Portal, Public Complaints — none of these modules exist in the base; they only illustrate how to map a domain onto the patterns.

nodes.label: Varnish Edge Cache (ADR-0042)
nodes.rationale: ETag/Last-Modified saves bandwidth but leaves DB load full; the in-process Redis layer still costs an app hop. Varnish answers repeated public requests without waking the application at all — zero DB load on a HIT.

nodes.label: Edge Cache Modes off/auto/on
nodes.rationale: The mode never changes WHAT may be cached, only for how long; off is genuinely inert (no headers, no queries).

nodes.label: PUBLIC_CACHE_SURFACES Registry
nodes.rationale: Each entry carries an anchored pattern, TTL, requiresTenant, an allow-listed query-param set and a mandatory rationale arguing why a SHARED cache may store it.

nodes.label: edge-cache:surfaces:check Gate
nodes.rationale: Rejects unanchored patterns, greedy wildcards, empty rationales and a bloated query allow-list, and probes 16 paths that must never be cacheable — it already caught /blog/{code}/search matching the three-segment blog-post pattern. It also rejects a surface whose owning module declares no serving route, and demands purge emission from every surface owner.

nodes.label: Purge Scope Key Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Keys are restricted to [A-Za-z0-9:._-] when built AND re-validated in the VCL, because the key goes into a regex — a `.*` would turn one invalidation into dumping the entire cache back to the origin.

nodes.label: Purge Outbox + Lease Worker
nodes.rationale: Content modules call enqueueEdgeCachePurge inside the same content transaction (ADR-0006 outbox); delivery is a worker with lease + retry over POST /__edge-cache-purge, because Bun cannot send the non-standard BAN method.

nodes.label: Three Bugs That Only Appeared When Run
nodes.rationale: All three passed review and bun run check and all three REPORTED SUCCESS while broken: literal spaces made every ban expression rejected; Bun sent BAN as GET so purges 404'd at the origin; and sql/068's RLS policy used a GUC nobody sets, so the awaited enqueue made publishing a post fail with 500. The fetchImpl mock inspects arguments, not the wire, so it could never catch bug 2 — the fix was a real Bun.serve asserting the method as RECEIVED.
nodes.norm_label: three bugs that only appeared when run

nodes.label: Purge Reaches Varnish Only, Not Cloudflare
nodes.rationale: Readers are actually served by Cloudflare, so a purge reporting done plus a Varnish MISS does not mean fresh content: staleness is bounded by s-maxage clamped to EDGE_CACHE_MAX_TTL_SECONDS — time, not invalidation. Recorded as gap C14.
nodes.norm_label: purge reaches varnish only, not cloudflare

nodes.label: Host-Hash Prerequisite Is Two Properties
nodes.rationale: vcl_hash must hash req.http.host AND must not return(lookup) — a custom sub that returns terminates the chain, so builtin.vcl's own vcl_hash never hashes req.url and every path on one host collapses into a single cache entry.

nodes.label: When the Tenant Is Published Is a Disclosure Question
nodes.rationale: Publishing the tenant before the not-found branch makes a resource-missing 404 carry Surrogate-Control while an unknown-host 404 carries private,no-store — answering 'is this hostname a live tenant?' from a single request. Publish only on the serving path.
nodes.norm_label: when the tenant is published is a disclosure question

nodes.label: An Inert Surface Is Worse Than No Surface
nodes.rationale: Three /news/** entries outlived their routes by days after ADR-0071. Harmless in effect, but a standing statement that a shared cache may store a path — and a gate reporting OK over 11 surfaces reads as coverage of 11 things, not 8.
nodes.norm_label: an inert surface is worse than no surface

nodes.label: Aggregate Surfaces Have Two Writers
nodes.rationale: Discovery config belongs to seo_distribution but its CONTENT is aggregated from every seo_facts provider, so a blog_content purge tagged m:blog_content would never reach /sitemap.xml. enqueueModuleContentPurge now also purges consuming modules that own a surface, read from the registry.

nodes.label: One Deployed Environment (ADR-0083)
nodes.rationale: A pre-production environment exists to rehearse against real data and traffic; this deployment has neither — it demonstrates the template. What would be staged is the template itself, validated by CI gates plus the Postgres integration suite. The cost, recorded rather than hidden: no pre-production rehearsal for sql/NNN.

nodes.label: A 200 Is Not Proof Production Is Alive
nodes.rationale: Verified 11 Aug 2026: the production application row was absent, no production database existed, and a staging Varnish container's two-host Traefik rule served the production domain from the staging database. The domain answered 200, healthy, throughout — so every direct measurement against it measured the wrong deployment.
nodes.norm_label: a 200 is not proof production is alive

nodes.label: Second-Environment Isolation Contract
nodes.rationale: Not a profile: the rule for ANY second environment, whatever it is called. Own database/role/password, own secrets, outbound integrations off, NEWS_PORTAL_PROFILE removed rather than re-valued, DNS provider manual, its own purge token. No APP_ENV value marks 'not the real one' — configuration separates them, not a label.

nodes.label: Coolify Creates POSTGRES_USER as Superuser
nodes.rationale: A superuser bypasses RLS unconditionally even with FORCE, so the deployment looks entirely healthy — green migrations, health 200, every endpoint working — while tenant isolation is absent.

nodes.label: NOLOGIN Roles Must Be Activated Explicitly
nodes.rationale: sql/019 and sql/022 create awcms_app/worker/setup NOLOGIN without passwords deliberately — a password is a secret and must not live in a migration. Green migrations therefore do NOT mean role separation is active. All three URLs are mandatory, or every job falls back to awcms_app and the separation becomes decoration.
nodes.norm_label: nologin roles must be activated explicitly

nodes.label: The 0 / 1 / 0 RLS Proof
nodes.rationale: Run as awcms_app: no tenant context → 0 rows, own tenant → 1, foreign tenant → 0. Without a tenant context the answer must be 0, not all rows — that is the difference between a policy that filters and one that is inert. The same queries as superuser pass while proving nothing.

nodes.label: Permission Seed Does Not Reach Existing Tenants
nodes.rationale: Seeds apply only to tenants created after them; symptom is a 403 on an already-installed module. A LEFT JOIN 'grant everything missing' cannot distinguish 'never existed at tenant creation' from 'deliberately revoked', so it resurrects removed grants without trace — the backfill command only grants permissions whose catalogue row is newer than the owner role.
nodes.norm_label: permission seed does not reach existing tenants

nodes.label: Local Development Brought In Line With Production
nodes.rationale: Before parity, dev was silently different — schema 40 migrations behind, zero tenants, and the only LOGIN role a superuser — so the most expensive bug classes (RLS leaks and permission 403s) were exactly the ones impossible to reproduce there. AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE/TRUSTED_PROXY_ENABLED/EDGE_CACHE_MODE stay deliberately different, each for a stated reason.
nodes.norm_label: local development brought in line with production

nodes.label: DATABASE_URL Serves Two Contradictory Roles
nodes.rationale: Runtime wants least-privilege awcms_app; the integration harness needs a privileged role to create ephemeral databases and ALTER ROLE. Override all three vars when testing — leaving SETUP_DATABASE_URL from .env makes the harness fail with 'Connection closed', a message that does not point at its cause.

nodes.label: Migrations as a One-Shot Container at the Release Tag
nodes.rationale: The runtime image ships no scripts/, so docker exec db:migrate fails. The checkout must be the DEPLOYED release tag, not main — main may hold sql/NNN absent from the image, and an applied migration is immutable. Git tag and image tag differ by the stripped leading v.
nodes.norm_label: migrations as a one-shot container at the release tag

nodes.label: Production Edge Cache in auto Mode
nodes.rationale: Topology Cloudflare → Traefik → varnish → app. Thresholds ≥5 req/s over 60s OR ≥250ms average origin latency, latched for 3× the window. Acceptance is measured with X-Cache and cf-cache-status, never an exit code.
nodes.norm_label: production edge cache in auto mode

nodes.label: Traefik Priority, Not Emptying the FQDN
nodes.rationale: Emptying the app FQDN requires a redeploy during which the Varnish backend disappears. Giving the Varnish router priority=100 makes the cache deterministic (otherwise the tie is arbitrary and traffic silently bypasses it) while keeping the app router as a zero-downtime fallback.
nodes.norm_label: traefik priority, not emptying the fqdn

nodes.label: Compression Is Inherited From Cloudflare, Not Owned
nodes.rationale: Zero compression middleware in the app, no beresp.do_gzip in the VCL, no Traefik compress middleware — only Vary: Accept-Encoding, a promise about caching rather than an act of compressing. A deployment NOT behind a compressing CDN serves everything uncompressed. The block is read by security:readiness, so deleting it turns that checker red.
nodes.norm_label: compression is inherited from cloudflare, not owned

nodes.label: APP_URL Is Not Cosmetic
nodes.rationale: It composes the OIDC/SSO callback URL, so a wrong host breaks login with redirect_uri_mismatch rather than merely producing an ugly link.

nodes.label: Same Identifier, Never the Same Password
nodes.rationale: awcms_identities is unique on (tenant_id, login_identifier), so one address in two environments is two accounts with two hashes; session tokens are tenant-scoped sha256 rows so they cannot cross. Copying passwords is the ONLY thing that can cancel that isolation. A prior claim about three AUTH_JWT_SECRETs was wrong — that variable does not exist.
nodes.norm_label: same identifier, never the same password

nodes.label: Tenant Subdomain DNS Root (Undecided Assumption)
nodes.rationale: Explicitly written as an assumption, not a decision. A second environment must leave the provider `manual`: two environments writing the same zone overwrite each other's serving records, a failure that makes no noise until production points somewhere wrong.

nodes.label: Eleven ERP Contract Families
nodes.rationale: Historical (ADR-0034/0055): the _shared contract files have been deleted and ERP is now a domain module in this repo. The base provided only neutral data shapes, one capability port and event payload schemas — never a chart of accounts.

nodes.label: BusinessTransactionReference & Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: A passive data type owned by the extension; externalTransactionId is opaque to the base and validating legalEntityScope is delegated to the business-scope contract.

nodes.label: Posting Request/Result Event Envelope
nodes.rationale: Idempotent per requestId, unique posted-state per (tenantId, transactionType, externalTransactionId) INDEPENDENT of requestId, 'accepted' is not proof of success, and reversalOfExternalTransactionId resolves an externalTransactionId — never a requestId — scoped to the reversal's tenant/legal entity.

nodes.label: Period-Lock Port (Fail-Closed)
nodes.rationale: The only new behavioural port. checked:false must be treated identically to locked:true for a post, and the base's only shipped adapter always returns checked:false — a composition root with no ERP extension gets a port that always refuses posting rather than one that silently permits it. It is not a replacement for RLS/ABAC.

nodes.label: Party Directory Port
nodes.rationale: Extension customer/supplier/employee tables store a profileId reference and never duplicate name/contact/identity data; the summary DTOs are an explicit allow-list, so raw email/phone is never exposed through this port. null means not-found — never display stale data.

nodes.label: BusinessScopeReference & Resolution
nodes.rationale: resolved:false (not an empty array) means the scope is not valid for that tenant, and the caller MUST default-deny — never treating 'no hierarchy' as 'permitted'.

nodes.label: Reconciliation Reference & Control Totals
nodes.rationale: matched/fullyReconciled are STRING-EXACT comparisons prepared by the caller; the contract does no numeric parsing or normalisation whatsoever.

nodes.label: Reporting Projection Contribution
nodes.rationale: The reporting engine NEVER reads an extension's ledger tables directly; the extension drives its read-model from its own events. requiredPermission must actually be enforced — do not repeat the 'descriptor field documented but not enforced' pattern.

nodes.label: Explicit ERP Exclusions
nodes.rationale: No chart of accounts, posting engine, valuation, orders, AR/AP, fixed assets, payroll or tax computation will ever exist in the base — and no claim that AWCMS is itself a compliant ERP.

nodes.label: Reversal-Target Security Review Note
nodes.rationale: The first fixture revision indexed the reversal target by requestId (the wrong ID space) and did not re-verify the resolved transaction's tenant/legal entity; both were fixed pre-merge. Do not cite the fixture as proven safe without reading that note.

nodes.label: Six Independent Versioning Schemes
nodes.rationale: Package release, REST contract, event contract, module descriptor contract, capability contract and manifest schema each change on their own schedule for their own reason; conflating them (e.g. assuming a release bump means the module contract changed) is the mistake this document exists to prevent.

nodes.label: MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH Bump Rule
nodes.rationale: An app built against an OLDER minor never breaks against a newer one, but declaring a HIGHER minor than shipped fails — it assumes a feature that does not exist yet. PATCH is never compatibility-checked.

nodes.label: Announce → Coexist → Remove Deprecation Policy
nodes.rationale: No fixed calendar SLA is imposed; the enforced guarantee is the MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH discipline — a MINOR release is never a surprise breaking change regardless of elapsed time since the announcement.

nodes.label: compatibleAwcmsRange Support-Window Guidance
nodes.rationale: Declare the NARROWEST range still useful, not the widest that passes today. An upper bound below the next MAJOR makes the gate fail loudly and early instead of subtly at runtime; widen only after actually verifying, never preemptively.

nodes.label: extension:check Enforcement (Cancelled)
nodes.rationale: Planned wiring into bun run check, the CI quality job and the preflight stage list so an incompatible manifest blocks something rather than appearing in a report nobody reads — CANCELLED by ADR-0034, not merely postponed.

nodes.label: AWCMS Family Contract Manifest
nodes.rationale: One declarative YAML at the repo root plus a JSON Schema, with family-contract.ts as the zero-import source of truth. Re-anchored by ADR-0055: it now declares the contracts this repo OWNS and that awcms-astro binds against, not conformance to an external mini standard.

nodes.label: FAMILY_CONTRACT_VERSION — the Seventh Scheme
nodes.rationale: MAJOR when a reusable control's semantics are WEAKENED or removed (default-deny, RLS, redaction, audit, idempotency, envelope, migration immutability) — every such change is breaking.

nodes.label: Validated Stack / Compatibility Matrix
nodes.rationale: Minimum-supported is actually RUN, not merely declared: the gate asserts the CI Bun version set is exactly {current, minimum} and that ciMinimum equals the engines floor, so deleting the minimum job or shifting the floor turns the gate red.

nodes.label: Intentional-Divergence Registry
nodes.rationale: Not a backlog of unfinished ports: each entry needs reason, owner, reviewDate (the gate fails once it is past) and an ADR file that must exist.

nodes.label: family:conformance:check Gate & Evidence Report
nodes.rationale: The report is built only from version strings and contract names and is asserted secret-free; a parity test keeps the CI step from silently dropping out.

nodes.label: Semantic, Mutation-Provable Contract Tests
nodes.rationale: Weakening a control turns the test red: a fail-open USING(true) policy leaks every row, a collapsed idempotency hash misses conflicts, a weakened redactor leaks, editing an applied migration throws. Part of the checklist is to MUTATE one contract and confirm the gate goes red before reverting.

nodes.label: Historical Divergences Archived by ADR-0055
nodes.rationale: Nine CI-gated entries were retired because 'is this difference from awcms-mini still justified?' is a question whose answer can no longer change; kept verbatim because their reasoning still explains why the code has its shape.

nodes.label: graphify-out/ Committed Knowledge Graph
nodes.rationale: One graph over the whole repo — code via AST, documents/contracts via semantic extraction — with graph.json, GRAPH_REPORT.md, manifest and cost tracked, and labels/visualisation/cache untracked.

nodes.label: graph:artifacts:check Gate
nodes.rationale: Holds the document to the node/edge/community counts and the tracked/untracked column — both were written true and had already gone false before the gate existed.

nodes.label: Finding Cross-Module Patterns With No Import
nodes.rationale: Its value is precisely what grep and modules:dag:check cannot find — e.g. it clustered 'anonymous surfaces answer uniformly, no oracle' across comments, self-registration and password-reset with no structural edge between them.
nodes.norm_label: finding cross-module patterns with no import

nodes.label: The Graph Mixes 'Was Once True' With 'Is True Now'
nodes.rationale: Nodes come from text including CHANGELOG and changesets, so an already-fixed bug still becomes a node and can surface as a live finding. Never use the graph to answer 'is X still true' — verify against the code first; the graph is a map, not the territory.
nodes.norm_label: the graph mixes 'was once true' with 'is true now'

nodes.label: Low Cohesion ≠ a Module That Needs Splitting
nodes.rationale: The largest community is 242 route handlers from 83 files plus withTenant and authorizeInTransaction — the fan-out shape of a deliberate chokepoint. A star topology inevitably scores near-zero cohesion; clustering cannot tell a hub from a loose cluster, and splitting it would break the security property most worth keeping.
nodes.norm_label: low cohesion = a module that needs splitting

nodes.label: Isolated-Node Gaps Are Mostly Noise
nodes.rationale: Most of the ~3400 isolated nodes are package.json keys, $schema, catalogue entries and leaf symbols — not undocumented components, and not a backlog.

nodes.label: TOTP Enrollment Flow
nodes.rationale: 20-byte CSPRNG secret stored encrypted as a pending factor; secret and the 10 recovery codes are shown ONCE, codes stored hash-only. Restarting enroll/start discards the previous pending secret so only the last QR is valid.

nodes.label: Two-Stage MFA Login
nodes.rationale: The MFA branch is reached only AFTER the password is valid, so it adds no enumeration oracle — unknown identifier, locked account and wrong password have already collapsed into one response. Every challenge deny path collapses to MFA_CHALLENGE_INVALID with identical response and timing.

nodes.label: requireStepUp Gate for High-Risk Actions
nodes.rationale: Called AFTER authorizeInTransaction; returns 403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED when the session is not aal2 or the step-up is stale. An aal1→aal2 rise revokes the old session and issues a new token (anti-fixation).

nodes.label: The Factor Belongs to the Human (ADR-0087)
nodes.rationale: Principal MFA tables are GLOBAL and without RLS because there is no tenant_id to compare against — one human really is one factor across their tenants. Challenges and tenant policies stay tenant-scoped under FORCE RLS: the factor belongs to the human, the obligation belongs to the tenant. The HTTP surface is unchanged; only storage moved.
nodes.norm_label: the factor belongs to the human (adr-0087)

nodes.label: Tenant MFA Enforcement Policy
nodes.rationale: required_for_privileged classifies broadly (any non-read permission) = fail-closed. A user owed MFA but holding no factor gets MFA_ENROLLMENT_REQUIRED plus a narrow grant token instead of a session — fail-closed but self-recoverable, with no admin lockout. Enforcement is inert if enrollment is disabled, because the demanded MFA would be impossible to create.

nodes.label: Tenant Selection/Switch Runs the Full Policy Gate
nodes.rationale: Without it, logging into a lax tenant A and switching to a strict tenant B would land an aal1 session — tenant switching becomes an MFA bypass, harming the strictest tenant most. Assurance does not travel: a session born of selection/switching is always aal1, because step-up is fresh proof for ONE tenant.
nodes.norm_label: tenant selection/switch runs the full policy gate

nodes.label: Cumulative Per-Factor Lockout
nodes.rationale: Independent of source IP and challenge rotation, so it catches an attacker minting new challenges while rotating IPs. Since ADR-0087 it is GLOBAL — the accepted trade-off comes with all three recovery levers (recovery codes, self-service disable + re-enrol, admin reset), which are now global too, so recovery is better than before.

nodes.label: Admin Reset Reaches Outside the Acting Tenant
nodes.rationale: The only place a tenant admin action changes state another tenant relies on. Recorded as crossTenantReach:true plus disabled_by_tenant_id — stating that it reaches outside WITHOUT saying where to, because a tenant list would be a cross-tenant membership oracle for anyone holding the reset permission (and FORCE RLS makes writing an audit row in the other tenant impossible anyway).
nodes.norm_label: admin reset reaches outside the acting tenant

nodes.label: Encryption Key Rotation Runbook
nodes.rationale: Only one key is active, so replacing it invalidates every stored secret (MFA_MISCONFIGURED). Zero-downtime rotation needs multi-key support that does not exist; until then rotation means a maintenance window with mass re-enrolment or a controlled mass disable.

nodes.label: Admin Recovery SOP & Break-Glass
nodes.rationale: Out-of-band identity verification first; a mandatory reason on a critical audit; self-reset forbidden; keep at least one MFA-enrolled admin per tenant so a reset is always possible, and say during verification that the reset is global.

nodes.label: MFA Threat Model
nodes.rationale: TOTP replay is closed by a strictly monotonic last_used_step advanced by compare-and-swap; recovery-code replay by UPDATE ... AND used_at IS NULL RETURNING — of two concurrent requests only one wins in each case.

nodes.label: MetricsPort Architecture
nodes.rationale: recordCounter/recordHistogram/recordGauge are the only official way to record; all three drop label keys not declared for that metric (defence in depth) and never let an adapter error escape. Metrics complement logging/audit and are NEVER a source of authorization.

nodes.label: No-Op Adapter as the Default
nodes.rationale: Every offline/LAN deployment that never calls setMetricsPort pays zero I/O and needs no collector — the 'runs without an external collector' requirement is satisfied by construction, not by a runtime check.

nodes.label: Shared Instrumentation Chokepoints
nodes.rationale: Provider/job/pool metrics flow through the mechanism that already exists rather than being duplicated per call site: buildResult in job-runner, decorateWithMetrics around the single provider breaker factory, and the one place work-class active/queue counts ever change.

nodes.label: METRIC_DEFINITIONS Registry
nodes.rationale: Every emitted metric must declare its complete label set, an approxCardinality estimate and a privacyNote.

nodes.label: Label Cardinality & Privacy Rule
nodes.rationale: No tenant id, id-bearing route, email/IP, object key, token, account/NPWP number, amount or conversation content in any label — every value must be a fixed enum member or code literal, never data from a request body or a tenant record.

nodes.label: deriveProviderFamilyLabel Bounding
nodes.rationale: A breaker registry key can be tenant-scoped, so putting it raw in a label would be BOTH a tenant-id leak and unbounded cardinality; keeping only the code-hardcoded prefix before the first ':' works because every call site follows the same literal-prefix convention.

nodes.label: Initial SLI/SLOs
nodes.rationale: Initial targets for an operations team to tune, not a contractual commitment; each SLI is computable from the declared metrics, and the burn-rate maths runs in the alerting backend rather than in this base.

nodes.label: Multi-Window Multi-Burn-Rate Alerting
nodes.rationale: Fast burn (>14.4x over 5m AND 1h) pages; slow burn (>1x–6x over 6h AND 3d) raises a ticket — the same two-window pattern applies to every SLO.

nodes.label: Authorized Dependency-Health Endpoint
nodes.rationale: Never exposes the raw breaker registry key — only the bounded family label; when several breakers map to one family the WORST state is reported, giving one aggregate signal and never a per-tenant breakdown.

nodes.label: The IdP Is an Authenticator, Not an Authority
nodes.rationale: After OIDC succeeds AWCMS mints its own opaque session and authorization still goes through RBAC/ABAC/RLS; the ID token is never used as the application session. Provider configuration is per-tenant DATA, so one deployment serves many tenants with different issuers.
nodes.norm_label: the idp is an authenticator, not an authority

nodes.label: SSO Start/Callback Flow
nodes.rationale: Tenant resolved before the flow and bound into state; state consumed single-use with FOR UPDATE + CAS; PKCE code_verifier server-side; an active MFA factor turns the callback into a challenge rather than a session.

nodes.label: ID Token Verification (Fail-Closed)
nodes.rationale: Algorithm allow-list {RS256, ES256} matched against the key type, WebCrypto signature, and issuer/audience/azp/expiry/iat/nonce all fail-closed; the linking key is the immutable sub, never email.

nodes.label: Explicit Account Linking With Step-Up
nodes.rationale: Linking is never automatic just because an email matches: it needs an authenticated session plus a fresh MFA step-up, and the identity_id is taken server-side from the session.

nodes.label: auto-link / JIT Account-Takeover Warning
nodes.rationale: Default OFF. Only safe for domains you fully control and IdPs you trust for email_verified — against a consumer or multi-organisation IdP, anyone able to hold email_verified:true for a colliding address turns this into a takeover primitive. JIT never overwrites an existing identity.

nodes.label: SSRF Guard on Tenant-Supplied Issuer URLs
nodes.rationale: HTTPS-only; blocks private/loopback/link-local/ULA/CGNAT/metadata IPv4+IPv6 including IPv4-mapped and NAT64; validates every DNS result before connecting, follows redirects manually with re-validation, caps time and size, and breaks per tenant+provider. Residual accepted: DNS rebinding after validation, bounded by the 30s negative cache and the breaker, not the 1h positive cache.
nodes.norm_label: ssrf guard on tenant-supplied issuer urls

nodes.label: Break-Glass Precondition
nodes.rationale: sso_required / password_login_enabled=false may only be stored when at least one currently-active break-glass identity exists, else 409. sso_required alone is ADVISORY — useful for UX, not enforcement. During an IdP outage the password path still works because it never touches the provider.

nodes.label: Break-Glass Control-Drift Readiness Check
nodes.rationale: A break-glass identity can be deactivated without the policy ever being saved again, so the save-time guarantee silently becomes false. checkSsoBreakGlassReady re-derives eligibility for every active tenant using the SAME functions as the save path — not a second copy of the rules — one transaction per tenant because the table is FORCE RLS, with no LIMIT.

nodes.label: SSO Data Minimization
nodes.rationale: Only sub+issuer (and email when linking requires it) is persisted; ID/access tokens are verified in memory and never stored; the client secret is ciphertext or an env reference and never appears in a response, log or audit.

nodes.label: Performance Suite Architecture
nodes.rationale: A target standard: seeded PRNG, scale profiles, pure fixture generator vs I/O seeder, pure metric aggregation, redaction, versioned query-plan budgets, and scenarios that REUSE the resilience scenario-runner types rather than a parallel runner.

nodes.label: Why a Representative Suite Is Needed
nodes.rationale: Ad hoc EXPLAIN ANALYZE plus one micro-benchmark proves nothing about multi-tenant scale, long-run memory stability, RLS plans at real volume, or interactive vs reporting workloads fighting over one connection pool.
nodes.norm_label: why a representative suite is needed

nodes.label: Deterministic Seeded Fixtures
nodes.rationale: Math.random and crypto.randomUUID never appear, and row TIMESTAMPS are computed from a seed-pure anchor rather than Date.now() — so the same (profile, seed) is byte-identical across runs, machines and calendar days, preserving release-to-release comparability. Strings come from a small fixed vocabulary, never resembling real identities or NPWP/NIK.

nodes.label: Fixture Seeding Goes Through withTenant
nodes.rationale: Seeding uses the same chokepoint as production mutations rather than a privileged bypass, so a freshly seeded database is real evidence that cross-tenant RLS negatives still hold at large data volume.

nodes.label: safe / standard / large Scale Profiles
nodes.rationale: The LAST tenant in every profile is the designated noisy neighbour with multiplied row counts — never an accidental scale, always the same deterministic position for a given seed.

nodes.label: Work-Class-Gated Workload Scenarios
nodes.rationale: Each workload is a REAL withTenant-gated operation mapped onto one of the five work classes, not a simulation.

nodes.label: saturation-and-recovery Scenario
nodes.rationale: The core proof: it does not simulate backpressure but genuinely over-subscribes the real bounded FIFO gate, asserts the exact count of immediate 503 DATABASE_BUSY + Retry-After rejections, then proves the gate drains to empty and follow-up calls succeed.

nodes.label: Versioned Query-Plan Regression Budgets
nodes.rationale: Plan SHAPE assertions plus numeric budgets with an explicit approval record. There is no env var or flag that loosens a budget — the only way to change one is a reviewed source diff. EXPLAIN runs under a real RLS connection inside a transaction that is always rolled back.

nodes.label: Two Independent Adversarial Proofs
nodes.rationale: A checker only ever tested against good input proves nothing. Forcing the planner GUCs off is the honest way to reproduce a missing index — an unindexed ILIKE is not enough, because RLS always injects tenant_id and every RLS-scoped table has a (tenant_id, …) prefixed index, so Postgres still picks an Index Scan.

nodes.label: Non-Overridable Production Target Guard
nodes.rationale: authorizeDrDrill is imported UNMODIFIED: APP_ENV=production is rejected with no override flag, the DATABASE_URL host must be on a default-deny allowlist, and --confirm-non-production is a mandatory typo-catcher.

nodes.label: Report Redaction & Environment Disclaimer
nodes.rationale: Three sequential passes — DSN at source, a DSN-shaped backstop over the whole tree, then a UUID-shaped backstop replaced by stable per-run pseudonyms. The report states explicitly that numbers are comparable release-to-release on the SAME environment only, never a universal production guarantee.

nodes.label: Safe Subset vs Full Lane
nodes.rationale: The safe subset runs every PR as awcms_app so RLS is genuinely enforced; the full lane is scheduled/manual only and NEVER wired into bun run check, because absolute wall-clock deltas are not a fair CI gate.

nodes.label: Post-Release Review Register
nodes.rationale: Deliberately separate from PROJECT_STATE §4: that register is bound to work ROUNDS and records decisions, this one is bound to RELEASES and records what happened in production. Before it existed the second had nowhere to go and was written as the first, or not at all. Written within a working week of the tag — long enough to see something, short enough to still remember.

nodes.label: A Smooth Release Still Gets an Entry
nodes.rationale: A register holding only incidents teaches its reader that releases are usually troubled and removes the baseline that makes a bad release look bad. It records what HAPPENED, not what was planned — the plan is already in the changeset and PR. Being empty and saying so beats being filled in backwards from memory.
nodes.norm_label: a smooth release still gets an entry

nodes.label: What a Template Can and Cannot Answer About Privacy
nodes.rationale: Legal basis, DPO appointment, processor agreements and cross-jurisdiction transfers are facts about the deployment and the organisation, not the code — a template pretending to answer them would sell the operator a sense of safety it bought them nothing.
nodes.norm_label: what a template can and cannot answer about privacy

nodes.label: Every Claim Points at a Gated Place
nodes.rationale: Not a writing style but the only reason the page can still be trusted in six months. It deliberately does NOT copy per-table retention numbers — such a copy goes stale the first day a descriptor changes, and a stale number in a privacy document is more dangerous than no number.
nodes.norm_label: every claim points at a gated place

nodes.label: Categories of Personal Data Held
nodes.rationale: Derived from the real schema rather than memory: identity/credentials, activity traces (audit, ABAC decision logs, sessions, salted-HMAC visitor hashes), and end-user-entered content the base cannot know the shape of.

nodes.label: Global Tables Without RLS and Their Substitutes
nodes.rationale: Principals and principal MFA tables are global (ADR-0085/0087); their isolation is not RLS but four substitute controls, one of which is a gate limiting which files may mention those tables at all.
nodes.norm_label: global tables without rls and their substitutes

nodes.label: REDACTION_KEYS Exact-Match Discipline
nodes.rationale: IP synonyms are matched EXACTLY rather than by substring, because a substring match would wreck ordinary fields like description and shipping.

nodes.label: Three Questions Every New Feature Must Answer
nodes.rationale: What new personal data, how long and what deletes it, and who can see it. 'None' is a valid and usually correct answer to the first — but it must be written down, not assumed; 'forever' is a decision that must be visible.
nodes.norm_label: three questions every new feature must answer

nodes.label: Data Subject Rights Position
nodes.rationale: #557 refused to build an export on top of a 139-table debt ledger, because an export answering with 3 tables and silent about 139 is a report signed and incomplete — worse than none. The ledger was paid to zero first. The export STATES its own coverage, naming deliberately unanswered tables, so a report that silently drops a global table is distinguishable from one written before that table existed.

nodes.label: Maker/Checker Erasure
nodes.rationale: The requester can never approve their own request, enforced in four layers (two permissions, a critical SoD rule, a CHECK constraint, one conditional UPDATE). Export and erasure are two different authorities: holding the right to read is not a reason to hold the right to destroy. The subject is answered per tenant because each tenant is a separate controller.

nodes.label: What Only the Operator Can Answer
nodes.rationale: Legal basis, controller/processor status, storage location and transfers, breach notification deadlines, and the retention actually chosen within the descriptor's min/max.
nodes.norm_label: what only the operator can answer

nodes.label: Preflight Is Read-Only by Default
nodes.rationale: Before the fix, db:migrate ran as an early unconditional stage, so a later failure still left the target migrated while the verdict said blocked — a preflight that mutates its target even when it blocks is not safe to run repeatedly, which defeats the point.

nodes.label: authorizeApply — Three Flags Together
nodes.rationale: Refuses unconditionally if any read-only stage failed — no flag combination overrides a failed quality gate. --acknowledge-target must match APP_ENV exactly as a typo-catcher, so the wrong shell produces a hard refusal rather than a silent mutation of the wrong database.

nodes.label: --backup-verified Is an Attestation, Not a Check
nodes.rationale: The operator attests to a specific evidence trail: a dump never test-restored is not verified evidence. The restore verifies the manifest HMAC, the checksum and the archive structure before touching any target, and defaults to a disposable database.
nodes.norm_label: --backup-verified is an attestation, not a check

nodes.label: Rehearsal Stage (Only Where a Second Environment Exists)
nodes.rationale: --acknowledge-target cannot distinguish a rehearsal database from the real one; only DATABASE_URL can, so read it back before pressing enter. The migration:plan list must match what was rehearsed EXACTLY. The DR drill must target a throwaway restore, because its interlock gives production no override — removing staging removed the one APP_ENV that was both production-like and drillable.
nodes.norm_label: rehearsal stage (only where a second environment exists)

nodes.label: Forward-Only Rollback Options
nodes.rationale: Preferred: restore the pre-apply backup. Leaving an additive migration applied and reverting the code is only acceptable once verified non-destructive — for posted ledger entries, payroll runs and stock movements, prefer restore whenever there is any doubt.

nodes.label: Per-Apply Evidence Retention
nodes.rationale: Dump + checksum, restore-test confirmation, the JSON preflight report, and a one-line rollback decision record; for financial/payroll modules statutory retention applies, not just operational convenience.

nodes.label: bun run security:readiness
nodes.rationale: A real implementation performing genuine RLS/RBAC-ABAC/secret/fail-closed inspection; exits non-zero if even a single critical check fails.

nodes.label: Named Check + Severity + Evidence Model
nodes.rationale: Every check yields name, severity, status and evidence, so the report can be read as an audit trail rather than a boolean.

nodes.label: config:validate Runs First of All
nodes.rationale: Configuration must be valid before any stage attempts a connection or a migration.

nodes.label: db:pool:health Exit Semantics
nodes.rationale: healthy/degraded exit 0, unhealthy exits non-zero, and a failed fetch is ALSO a hard failure with a clear message — never silently looking like a pass.

nodes.label: production:preflight Orchestrator (Not Yet Built)
nodes.rationale: Every stage still runs after a failure (not fail-fast) so one failure cannot hide another; db:pool:health is recorded as skipped rather than failed when no server answers, so preflight is runnable in CI; bun install is deliberately excluded as environment setup, not a readiness check.

nodes.label: Explicitly Out-of-Scope Readiness Items
nodes.rationale: Printed explicitly in the report — not hidden, and not forced into a fake check. Tax and payroll/HR masking are IN scope for AWCMS (unlike the generic base) and need dedicated checks once those modules exist, rather than documentation saying 'a derived domain'.

nodes.label: Known Readiness Gaps
nodes.rationale: Checks needing a real Postgres are not unit-tested against a fake DB — that would test the mock, not the query; their proof must be live verification including deliberately turning RLS off to show the gate blocks, rather than a script that always prints pass. Security headers are checked for presence only, and the login rate limiter is per-process.

nodes.label: Global Principal (awcms_principals)
nodes.rationale: One human, one credential, many tenants. Executed as a promotion of authority that moves no foreign key: awcms_identities keeps its id and its eight FKs, a nullable principal_id is added, and resolveTenantContext/authorizeInTransaction never learn principals exist. Global without RLS is defensible only because 'a principal is an AUTHENTICATION fact, never an AUTHORIZATION fact' — four controls replace RLS (never DELETE, an allow-listed keyed-read gate, password_hash never leaves the store module, authorization still through awcms_tenant_users under FORCE RLS).

nodes.label: Cloudflare Isomorphism Map
nodes.rationale: Cloudflare is used as a MODEL, not an integration target: the partner Tenant API needs a signed agreement, so what is pursued is a membership model isomorphic with Cloudflare's, making a future integration a table mapping rather than a redesign. One difference is deliberately NOT adopted: Cloudflare's effective permission is purely additive, AWCMS keeps ABAC deny-overrides — union applies only on the grant side.

nodes.label: awcms_access_policies (a grant carries its own scope)
nodes.rationale: A NEW table rather than extending awcms_access_assignments: the UNIQUE (tenant_id, tenant_user_id, role_id) is exactly what must die, extending business_scope_assignments would force rewriting the two SoD readers in the same PR, and a third table makes expand/migrate/contract possible without dual-write. Six composite FKs carrying tenant_id are mandatory because PostgreSQL runs referential integrity as the table owner and bypasses RLS.
nodes.norm_label: awcms_access_policies (a grant carries its own scope)

nodes.label: User Groups (awcms_user_groups)
nodes.rationale: Groups GRANT ROLES, never permissions directly — otherwise a policy matching subject.roles silently stops matching (a deny becoming inert, which is a widening) and SoD stops seeing group-derived grants. external_id is the sync key, not group_code, so an IdP rename cannot orphan a group. SCIM is not built, only not obstructed.

nodes.label: Invitations (awcms_invitations)
nodes.rationale: The invitation carries its own Policy, exactly like Cloudflare. Resend rotates the token (without rotation, resend is a token-multiplication surface); an expired token answers 404 not 410 so no status oracle exists; skip_email_confirmation is platform-scoped so no tenant admin can mint an unverified GLOBAL principal for someone else's address. Invitations and self-registration both stay because their directions are opposite (push vs pull).

nodes.label: Entitlement Layer (SaaS plans & subscriptions)
nodes.rationale: Lands inert (zero descriptors declare requiresEntitlement) with a golden test proving the guard chain is byte-identical. ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED sits AFTER module_disabled (a tenant that turned its own module off deserves that answer, not an upgrade offer) and is hard-exempt for the platform tenant, so an overdue subscription cannot lock the operator out of its own control plane. Backfill is acceptable as a blanket migration only because an entitlement never existed to be revoked.

nodes.label: Quota is Admission Control, Not Authorization
nodes.rationale: Four reasons, none sufficient alone: a quota is mutated by the action being authorized so it needs SELECT FOR UPDATE in the same write transaction the chokepoint cannot hold; counting resources would force identity_access to import every module's schema (forbidden by ADR-0011); writing deny rows for a capacity condition poisons the decision log as a security signal; and 409 QUOTA_EXCEEDED is actionable where 403 ACCESS_DENIED is not. Capability (boolean) at the chokepoint, volume through a quota port.
nodes.norm_label: quota is admission control, not authorization

nodes.label: Delegated Access Grant
nodes.rationale: An approved grant mints an ordinary awcms_tenant_users row bound to a limited support role, so RLS, decision log, audit, SoD and business-scope facts work unchanged — the actor genuinely IS a tenant user there. The grant row is RLS'd on the TARGET tenant (the customer's view is authoritative); the partner's view goes through a narrow SECURITY DEFINER function. Derived sessions are switchable=false with a bounded TTL and die with the grant.

nodes.label: A Partner Is an Ordinary Tenant
nodes.rationale: ModulePermissionScope stays {tenant, platform}; there is no 'partner' value. Scope governs who may HOLD a permission, partnership governs WHICH OBJECTS it touches — merging them produces a permission held correctly and executed against the wrong tenant, and no RLS policy would object because the actor is legitimately authenticated somewhere. Reach is data, not permission.
nodes.norm_label: a partner is an ordinary tenant

nodes.label: Chokepoint Step Order Invariant
nodes.rationale: The structural gates (machine-credential, module_disabled, entitlement_required, platform_scope_required, tenant_suspended) MUST sit above fetchGrantedPermissionKeys — all answer 'the caller's grants must not influence this'. Moving any below turns a structural gate into a permission-shaped one and the failure is invisible: one grant row that should not exist becomes sufficient. Claims of the form 'X runs before Y' must be tested at SOURCE level and be rename-proof.

nodes.label: Suspended as a Service Status
nodes.rationale: Today suspension is read only on login/reset/registration/SSO-start and the public host resolver: the public site dies immediately while already-issued admin sessions keep full access and machine credentials are untouched. The fix is a 403 TENANT_SUSPENDED deny branch before the permission lookup, with the still-alive action allow-list written as a constant commented 'widening this needs an ADR'.

nodes.label: Principal Token (never authenticates the chokepoint)
nodes.rationale: The most dangerous invariant in the program: the bearer kind is carried by its hash namespace, isPrincipalTokenHash() is checked BEFORE resolveTenantContext, and a principal hash produces a hard 401 with zero decision log rows. Paired with the non-switchable rule — a session born from a tenant IdP or break-glass must be switchable=false, or the IdP admin of tenant B could assert a user and then switch into tenant A.

nodes.label: fetchGrantedPermissionKeys
nodes.rationale: Keeps its NAME because the chokepoint gate locks onto that literal; only its return type changes to {keys, scopes}. Its body becomes a UNION ALL over three tables so that with the new table empty the result is exactly today's data, verified by a differential oracle over a random subject corpus while both sources are alive.

nodes.label: access:chokepoint:check gate
nodes.rationale: A gate that will NOT go red even though it should: renaming fetchGrantedPermissionKeys leaves it green while reporting '0 handlers decide a permission'. PR 0.2 adds a deciding.length > 0 assertion plus structural (not variable-name) assertions for exactly that.

nodes.label: loadAdminScreen
nodes.rationale: Named 'load' not 'define' because .astro frontmatter has no handler to wrap, so 'define' would promise a shape that does not exist. It mirrors defineTenantRoute: one withTenant, authorizeInTransaction and load inside the SAME transaction — a second transaction would break decision/read atomicity and miss the scope filter. A deny renders a denied state, not a redirect, because 20+ page-contract tests assert ids like #users-denied.

nodes.label: ABAC Decision Log Retention
nodes.rationale: ~8.6 million rows/day at 100 rps with no retention at all, while the same table is the cursor source for the reporting projection whose description calls it 'append-only — never deleted'. Retention and projection authority are ONE decision, not two; sql/022 granted only SELECT so today's purge job cannot delete.

nodes.label: data-lifecycle:table-coverage:check
nodes.rationale: Planned as a HIGH-VOLUME gate; three ways of deriving 'high volume' from repo artifacts were built and all three failed (append-only at source = 46 tables, no delete path = 94, unbounded-by-schema = 121 of 128). A gate whose exception list is 90% of the schema is a hand-written list in disguise, so the question was replaced: a table EXISTS therefore it must carry a dataLifecycle descriptor or a reasoned exception, with a legacy ledger that may only shrink.

nodes.label: Machine Credential Write Classes
nodes.rationale: The ceiling stays IN CODE, intersected with the per-credential column: as a pure column, one backup restore or one hand-written INSERT could mint a catalogue-wide write credential with every gate green. IP conditions must DENY when clientIp is unavailable, and the machine_credential_readonly sentinel is kept verbatim because it exists in decision log history.

nodes.label: Bun-native RedisClient
nodes.rationale: Uses Bun's native client so no redis/ioredis runtime package is added and bun.lock does not change. No hidden fallback: Bun's built-in `redis` singleton (which can point at localhost automatically) is never used — the client is created explicitly only when REDIS_ENABLED=true and REDIS_URL is valid.

nodes.label: Cache-aside with mandatory TTL and fail-open
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL stays authoritative; a Redis outage becomes a cache miss, a write skip, or an invalidation skip, never a failed business transaction. TTL is mandatory (atomic SET ... EX) so a failed invalidation is bounded by expiry, and Redis is never a mandatory dependency inside a PostgreSQL transaction. Never build a PostgreSQL+Redis dual write as a pseudo-transaction — the two have no shared atomic commit.
nodes.norm_label: cache-aside with mandatory ttl and fail-open

nodes.label: buildRedisKey (tenant-aware keys)
nodes.rationale: Tenant data must carry tenantId in the key; REDIS_KEY_PREFIX doubles as the application namespace and the ACL key boundary.

nodes.label: redis:health preflight command
nodes.rationale: Four statuses (disabled/healthy/unhealthy/invalid_configuration); URL credentials are always redacted and cache payloads are never printed.

nodes.label: Forbidden Redis Uses Without a New Design
nodes.rationale: Redis must not be the single source of sessions, audit/security events, outbox/inbox, workflow approvals, ledgers/stock/payroll, RLS/RBAC/ABAC replacement, an exactly-once queue, or a store for passwords/tokens/NIK/PII. Changing any of those requires its own issue, threat model, data classification, RTO/RPO and failure testing.
nodes.norm_label: forbidden redis uses without a new design

nodes.label: Hardened Standalone Redis Deployment
nodes.rationale: Provided as a separate deployment because AWCMS has no canonical root Compose stack; default user disabled, awcms_app restricted to the key prefix, ACL file holds only the password hash, no published port, cap_drop ALL and no-new-privileges.

nodes.label: changesets:policy:check
nodes.rationale: Runs as its own workflow rather than inside ci.yml's quality job or bun run check, because it is inherently PR-diff shaped (it needs the origin/main tip); every other check step is self-contained against a single checkout. Exempt: docs/**, .claude/**, .changeset/**, any *.md — everything else including .github/**, scripts/**, sql/** requires a changeset.

nodes.label: release.yml workflow
nodes.rationale: Two entry points converge on one job graph: a v*.*.* tag push (real release) and workflow_dispatch (rehearsal against dryrun-<sha>). The rehearsal is not a shortcut around the quality gate — it only skips the tag-ancestor guard and release:verify. The image tag drops the v prefix while the git tag and GitHub Release keep it.

nodes.label: sign-attest-publish job
nodes.rationale: Split out of build for a security reason: id-token/attestations permissions are JOB-scoped, so every step in a job holding them can mint its own OIDC token. Keeping the third-party anchore/sbom-action entirely out of this job means a supply-chain compromise of that action never has OIDC/attestation credentials to abuse. Signing is keyless OIDC — no signing key ever exists.

nodes.label: Dual CycloneDX SBOM (anchore/sbom-action)
nodes.rationale: Two SBOMs because source tree and built image legitimately differ (the image also reflects base-image OS packages). Syft is a statically-linked Go binary that never executes project code and never invokes npm — npm-ecosystem SBOM generators would conflict with the Bun-only rule; one action covers both scan targets so only one third-party action must be pinned and audited.

nodes.label: release Environment Approval Gate
nodes.rationale: Referencing an environment auto-creates an UNPROTECTED record — that alone does not pause anything; required reviewers are a repo-admin change deliberately left to a maintainer. On v6.0.0 the job ran with no pause because no reviewers existed; the gap was closed and proven by a rehearsal that stopped at status: waiting.

nodes.label: Rehearsal / dry-run path
nodes.rationale: Runs the pipeline in full against a throwaway dryrun-<sha> tag; never creates a GitHub Release and never moves :latest, so it cannot become a production release by accident. Old rehearsal images are deleted manually because automatic deletion would need packages: delete, a permission no job here needs.

nodes.label: release:verify
nodes.rationale: Checks the pushed tag's version against package.json, that CHANGELOG.md has its section, and that no unconsumed changesets remain. Paired with the ancestor-of-main guard, which substitutes for branch protection: a tag whose commit is not in origin/main's history is rejected before anything is built.

nodes.label: Rollback / Yank Guidance
nodes.rationale: Never delete a published tag/Release/image — consumers may already have pulled it and deleting removes their ability to diagnose. Mark pre-release, cut a new patch, and never force-push a corrected tag over the same version: the already-published digest and attestations would point at different bytes than the tag implies, defeating the whole checksum/signature/provenance chain.

nodes.label: Post-release Review (step 18)
nodes.rationale: A smooth release still gets an entry: a register containing only incidents teaches readers that releases are usually troubled and removes the baseline that makes a bad release look bad.

nodes.label: Repo Assessment 4 August 2026
nodes.rationale: A snapshot measured against four axes (AWCMS standards, the awcms-astro relationship, international performance and security standards). Every finding carries its file and line because this repo has a history of findings written from guesswork that were then copied into decisions; a snapshot must not be edited afterwards or it stops being a snapshot.

nodes.label: P0: Three Handlers Bypass the Authorization Chokepoint
nodes.rationale: First written as ONE route with blog/posts/[id].ts named as the CORRECT pattern — wrong, because a FILE-level reading merged GET/DELETE (which do call the guard) with PATCH (which does not). A per-HANDLER analysis of 331 handlers found three violators. Severity is moderate not critical: what leaks is policy consistency, not data — an ABAC deny honoured on one route and silently ignored on another. It is the class that is serious, not the instance.
nodes.norm_label: p0: three handlers bypass the authorization chokepoint

nodes.label: ownershipGrant (widens, never short-circuits)
nodes.rationale: The ownership rule becomes an INPUT to the chokepoint rather than a replacement, so ABAC deny, platform-scope, business-scope and SoD can still deny. The gate slices per HANDLER with exceptions keyed <file>#<METHOD> so they cannot widen to a neighbouring handler.

nodes.label: In-process Rate Limiter Does Not Hold Across Instances
nodes.rationale: With N replicas the effective limit becomes N x the configured limit, so the deployments that need protection most are the weakest. Closed by ADR-0066: Redis counts with the window number in the KEY so instances agree without read-modify-write, and it FAILS OPEN — stated bluntly because the per-identity lockout in PostgreSQL is unaffected.
nodes.norm_label: in-process rate limiter does not hold across instances

nodes.label: Unguarded awcms-astro Consumer Contract
nodes.rationale: The frozen OpenAPI snapshot predates migration #182, so none of the surfaces awcms-astro actually consumes are in it: changing their response shape is green here and breaks the other repo's build, where the person who changed it does not look. A second snapshot was added rather than widening the first, which has a different job and must stay frozen.

nodes.label: db:fk-index:check (first performance gate)
nodes.rationale: Tenant-aware: (tenant_id, fk) counts as reachable, because the literal 'must lead' rule is violated by 40 of 182 columns — and a gate demanding 40 migrations on the day it lands is an exception list waiting to be written.

nodes.label: Per-endpoint Query Budget
nodes.rationale: The 40-post fixture is deliberately larger than the ceiling: a ceiling over a single row proves nothing because an N+1 and a constant implementation both emit about one query. Mutation-proven by injecting a real N+1, and one test guards the counting Proxy itself so a broken instrument cannot make every ceiling pass vacuously.

nodes.label: Core Web Vitals Never Measured
nodes.rationale: Not a defect but an ADDITION of data collection about real visitors, colliding with the privacy-first posture visitor_analytics already states. ADR-0067 records three options; not taking it is a legitimate answer, better recorded as a decision than left as an open gap. Lab measurement was never weighed there and answers a different question from RUM.

nodes.label: AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE Fails Open When Unset
