nodes.label: /admin/reporting (src/pages/admin/reporting.astro)
nodes.rationale: Every mutation goes through the real /api/v1/reports/* endpoints — no privileged shortcut, no SQL in the page; five send a fresh per-click Idempotency-Key and reconcile sends none.

nodes.label: Historical doc section describing screens that never existed
nodes.rationale: The text came over with the port and was never true here; the module declared no navigation entry, so the registry gate that catches a dangling path had nothing to check — docs are not gated the way descriptors are.
nodes.norm_label: historical doc section describing screens that never existed

nodes.label: seo_distribution module
nodes.rationale: Consumer/aggregator of SEO facts, never a provider: content modules provide seo_facts and this module composes them, so nothing in the base registry depends on it and the module DAG is untouched.

nodes.label: ADR-0071 (public URL vocabulary split: /blog here, /news in awcms-astro)
nodes.norm_label: adr-0071 (public url vocabulary split: /blog here, /news in awcms-astro)

nodes.label: seo_facts capability port (_shared/ports/seo-facts-port.ts)
nodes.rationale: Only one module may declare provides: [seo_facts] at a time (capability_provider_conflict); a future content type ships its own adapter and seo_distribution never learns that type exists. Registered at 1.1.0 in _shared/capability-contract-versions.ts.

nodes.label: application/seo-metadata-service.ts (composition point)
nodes.rationale: Ports are plain parameters wired at the route composition root; the module's application/domain import no content module.

nodes.label: application/resolve-canonical-host.ts
nodes.rationale: Canonical/OG/hreflang host is always the tenant's verified primary domain, never a request header (host-header poisoning defense); with no primary domain it degrades to a relative canonical rather than inventing a host, and absolute-URL documents (sitemaps, feeds) 404 instead.

nodes.label: renderControlledJsonLd
nodes.rationale: Injection blocked by a closed @type/key schema plus escaping, not ad-hoc sanitization; it is the only path that emits JSON-LD, and only for indexable resources.

nodes.label: isPubliclyResolvable / isPubliclyIndexable
nodes.rationale: Every visibility decision delegates to these frozen guards; there is no code path that emits an unpublished resource to public output.

nodes.label: Public discovery surfaces (robots.txt, sitemap, RSS/Atom/JSON feeds)
nodes.rationale: Tenant-wide noindex suppresses ALL of them, not just robots.txt, so scrapers that ignore robots get no machine-readable URL enumeration; sitemap <loc>s only exist for a route family the tenant actually serves — an empty sitemap beats one full of certain 404s.
nodes.norm_label: public discovery surfaces (robots.txt, sitemap, rss/atom/json feeds)

nodes.label: domain/discovery-cache.ts (ETag/Last-Modified signature)
nodes.rationale: Signature over kind+tenantId+host+locale+contractVersion+configFingerprint+content roll-up, NUL-joined so free-text parts cannot merge across their boundary and tenantId isolates tenants sharing the null-host sentinel; because validators derive from state, any publish/update/domain/config change invalidates the output.

nodes.label: withSeoPublicTenant (public tenant resolution)
nodes.rationale: Every non-serving outcome is one generic, latency-normalized 404 (padUnresolvedSeoTenantLatency); host is trusted only behind PUBLIC_TRUST_PROXY and lookup is gated by PUBLIC_TENANT_RESOLUTION_MODE.

nodes.label: awcms_seo_redirects (exact-path redirect rules)
nodes.rationale: Resolved in middleware on the non-/admin branch before content routing, excluding admin/API/auth/static/system/discovery paths enforced at both resolve and write time; chains are bounded, non-recursive, and fail closed on loop or over-cap.

nodes.label: domain/redirect-target-classification.ts (open-redirect guard)
nodes.rationale: Re-homed as a standalone domain helper rather than re-added to the seo_facts port; every target passes it on write AND on every resolve.

nodes.label: The one invasive middleware edit is FAIL-OPEN
nodes.rationale: The resolver swallows all faults to null (never a 500) and the 404 capture never throws; the /admin guard and API body ceiling are untouched.
nodes.norm_label: the one invasive middleware edit is fail-open

nodes.label: awcms_seo_not_found_observations (privacy-minimized 404 telemetry)
nodes.rationale: Aggregate rows only — sanitized path plus bare referrer domain — with an analytics_telemetry dataLifecycle descriptor (30d default) and a SELECT, DELETE grant to awcms_worker.

nodes.label: domain/retired-news-redirect.ts (/news/** -> /blog/{tenantCode}/**)
nodes.rationale: Inverted from the old direction and deliberately NOT policy-gated: the routes are gone for everyone so there is nothing to opt into, and gating it on the module being enabled would break exactly the tenants who disabled it. One condition survives — a tenant without /blog/** gets no redirect, because a 301 to a guaranteed 404 is the failure ADR-0059 §C existed to prevent.

nodes.label: legacy_blog_redirect_enabled — retired but not dropped
nodes.rationale: Applied migrations are checksummed and immutable and its API surface has shipped, so nothing reads it and the correction lives in the README and domain/redirect-settings.ts instead of in sql/060.

nodes.label: Permission seed reaches only tenants created after the migration
nodes.rationale: sql/058 seeds seo_distribution.config.{read,update} into the global catalog, so pre-existing tenants need a functional (not security) backfill release step.
nodes.norm_label: permission seed reaches only tenants created after the migration

nodes.label: awcms_site_search_documents (tsvector/GIN index)
nodes.rationale: A projection of every content module's currently-public rows; publication state is enforced at the source->index boundary and the index is NEVER an authorization source.

nodes.label: SearchSourceDescriptor contribution seam
nodes.rationale: Pure data: column mapping, a declarative publication filter, a URL template and a weight. There is no executable extractor and no tenant SQL — only reviewed identifiers matching ^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$ are interpolated, exactly like data_lifecycle's generic executionMode.

nodes.label: domain/search-source-registry.ts + site-search:sources:check
nodes.rationale: Aggregates and validates every module's descriptors through listModules(); deliberately NOT modeled as a search_source capability, because more than one provider would trip capability_provider_conflict.

nodes.label: reconcile / rebuild / reindex indexing operations
nodes.rationale: All idempotent: reconcile upserts the current public set (checksum-gated) and deletes stale documents, rebuild deletes then reconciles to an identical end state, reindex is the event-shaped single-resource primitive. The scheduled sweep is the deterministic backbone because blog_content publishes lifecycle as log lines, not real outbox events.

nodes.label: /search page + /api/v1/site-search/{query,suggest}
nodes.rationale: The typeahead ARIA combobox was NOT ported: this base's CSP has no 'unsafe-inline' for scripts and public pages are plain APIRoute HTML with no bundling step, so the page ships no-JS core search and /suggest stays for a theme's client.

nodes.label: renderSafeSnippet (ts_headline sentinels)
nodes.rationale: Snippets are built with non-HTML sentinels, escaped, and only then turned into <mark>, so content-originated markup can never survive.

nodes.label: buildSearchCacheKey
nodes.rationale: Refuses a key without tenant/locale/query-hash — cache-poisoning and cross-tenant defense on top of RLS FORCE and explicit tenant_id/locale predicates.

nodes.label: Public URL safety via encodeURIComponent at index time
nodes.rationale: :tenantCode/:slug/:id are encoded when the document is written, so no source value can inject a path segment or a scheme; the awcms port also swapped the host-resolved /news/:slug URL for the path-tenant-scoped /blog/:tenantCode/:slug shape.
nodes.norm_label: public url safety via encodeuricomponent at index time

nodes.label: awcms_sync_nodes
nodes.rationale: Nodes auto-register on first contact but now as INACTIVE (advisory GHSA-c972-3q5p-g3h4) — an admin must approve them, which quarantines a forged first-contact node id for another tenant.

nodes.label: awcms_sync_outbox (RETIRED, sql/099)
nodes.rationale: It never had a producer, and the real question was not how to fill it but whether a second outbox should exist at all when awcms_domain_events already is one.

nodes.label: ADR-0077 (one outbox — sync pull reads domain events)
nodes.norm_label: adr-0077 (one outbox — sync pull reads domain events)

nodes.label: domain/sync-replication.ts replicable-event allow-list
nodes.rationale: Ships empty, so /sync/pull still answers with an empty list — but now because of a policy written in one place rather than a missing wire.

nodes.label: Payload projection + commit-visibility blockers
nodes.rationale: A node is HMAC-authenticated, not a session, so each replicable type needs its owning module to declare which fields travel — redactEventPayloadForResponse masks exactly what a replica needs. And event_sequence is assigned at INSERT but visible at COMMIT, so a cursor sequence > checkpoint can skip a late-committing event; replication should ride appendDomainEvent's delivery row instead of repeating the cursor.

nodes.label: awcms_sync_conflicts + conflict resolution endpoints
nodes.rationale: Immutable records — only the resolution columns are ever filled. Unlike the other sync endpoints these are session-authenticated, because conflict resolution is a human decision, not a node action.

nodes.label: awcms_sync_aggregate_versions (optimistic concurrency)
nodes.rationale: A generic evaluator with no domain knowledge of what the aggregate represents; conflicting events land in sync_conflicts rather than sync_inbox and do not advance the version.

nodes.label: HMAC node-to-node authentication
nodes.rationale: Machine-to-machine endpoints carry no bearer/session; a deployment-wide secret is verified timing-safe against a max skew for anti-replay, and X-AWCMS-Tenant-ID is required for isolation.

nodes.label: Signature v2 (tenant + node inside the signed material)
nodes.rationale: tenantId must be a UUID at the v2 boundary: nodeCode may contain ':' so a non-UUID tenantId makes the tenant/node boundary ambiguous; a UUID is fixed 36 chars with no ':', and both compute and verify fail closed otherwise.
nodes.norm_label: signature v2 (tenant + node inside the signed material)

nodes.label: Signature v1 (legacy, cross-tenant forgeable)
nodes.rationale: Binds neither tenant nor node and is kept only so deployed nodes keep working during migration; the advisory is only fully closed when SYNC_HMAC_ALLOW_LEGACY=false AND every node is on v2.

nodes.label: awcms_object_sync_queue
nodes.rationale: Re-enqueuing the same objectKey upserts rather than duplicating; requires_upload is set from R2_ENABLED at enqueue time as a data flag, never a network trigger (ADR-0006).

nodes.label: dispatchObjectSyncQueue (application/object-dispatch.ts)
nodes.rationale: Three-phase CLAIM/UPLOAD/FINALIZE required by ADR-0006, reusing next_retry_at as the claim lease with no new column. Naturally idempotent: sent/failed rows are never re-claimed and the objectKey is itself the dedup key, since an S3/R2 PUT to the same key is an overwrite.

nodes.label: infrastructure/object-storage-uploader.ts
nodes.rationale: createNoopObjectUploader touches no network when R2 is off; createR2ObjectUploader uses Bun's native S3Client with no npm SDK and re-verifies the local file's sha256 before uploading. A per-provider circuit breaker skips only requires_upload=true rows.

nodes.label: evaluateObjectRetry (domain/object-queue.ts)
nodes.rationale: Exponential 2^retryCount backoff capped at 60 minutes and ineligible after 5 retries; verifyObjectChecksum uses plain string equality because a checksum is not a secret.

nodes.label: /admin/sync operator console
nodes.rationale: None of its three mutations sends an Idempotency-Key because none of the endpoints requires one — they are naturally idempotent state transitions — and a contract test pins that in BOTH directions. The HMAC node protocol gets no controls here at all: those authenticate a node by signature, so a button would be a control no browser can legitimately use.

nodes.label: awcms_tenants (RLS-free multi-tenant root)
nodes.rationale: Because it is RLS-free, endpoints must carry an explicit WHERE id = <tenantId>.

nodes.label: Setup wizard (application/platform-bootstrap.ts)
nodes.rationale: One transaction claims the lock, creates tenant/settings/head office/owner profile+identity+tenant_user, mints the system owner role holding every permission existing at that moment, assigns it, and locks setup permanently.

nodes.label: Offices API (keyset-paginated)
nodes.rationale: At most 100 rows newest-first with an opaque nextCursor; a corrupt cursor is a 400, never a silent page 1.

nodes.label: Office soft-delete + restore
nodes.rationale: Restore is guarded by office_management.update, not delete and not a separate restore action: un-deleting is an edit to the record's lifecycle, the same authority as changing an office. restoreOffice reads office_code before the UPDATE to name the duplicate error precisely and to double as the existence check.

nodes.label: Composite FK (tenant_id, parent_office_id) — GHSA-r7cx-c4jh-cvvw
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL runs referential integrity with the table owner's rights and BYPASSES RLS, so an FK to id alone let tenant A parent an office under tenant B and turned the field into an existence oracle. RLS limits what a query may SELECT, not what a constraint may reference; the application check adds what no FK can express (a soft-deleted parent), and all three bad-parent causes fail identically.

nodes.label: withTenant transaction wrapper
nodes.rationale: It COMMITs when the callback returns normally, so a route that catches an error inside the transaction and returns 4xx PERSISTS whatever was written before the throw — the parent check must precede the first write, and after catching 23505 nothing may be written again or the 409 becomes a 25P02 500.

nodes.label: admin/offices.astro
nodes.rationale: All UI gates are UX only — the authority remains the endpoint guard; the script is bundled externally to stay CSP-safe.

nodes.label: tenant_domain module
nodes.rationale: Additive: ADR-0009's path-based /blog/{tenantCode} routing is untouched and src/middleware.ts is not modified, so the login/Turnstile/CSP guarantees are unchanged — host resolution is a per-public-route concern.

nodes.label: awcms_tenant_domains (migration 046)
nodes.rationale: The unique index on normalized_hostname WHERE deleted_at IS NULL is GLOBAL across tenants — a hostname maps to at most one tenant, and a soft delete frees it for reuse. verification_token_hash is an internal bearer hash never selected by any code; no column ever stores a DNS provider credential.

nodes.label: awcms_resolve_tenant_domain_lookup (SECURITY DEFINER, migration 048)
nodes.rationale: Owned by a dedicated NOLOGIN/NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS role with a scoped FOR SELECT policy; EXECUTE revoked from PUBLIC and granted only to awcms_app, and reserved for the anonymous public resolver — the management API never goes through it.

nodes.label: Tenant domain management API
nodes.rationale: hostname is immutable after create, is_primary is never settable through PATCH (only the atomic set-primary), PATCH can never set status active (use verify); a duplicate hostname is a generic 409 that never reveals whether it belongs to another tenant, and unknown/cross-tenant/deleted ids are a generic 404.

nodes.label: resolvePublicTenantFromRequest (the public host resolver seam)
nodes.rationale: Ordered resolution: tenant_code_legacy opts out entirely, then host lookup, then PUBLIC_DEFAULT_TENANT_ID/CODE, then setup_state, then null. Only an active domain on an active tenant resolves; every other case returns an identical null in exactly one DB round trip, so there is no timing side-channel. X-Forwarded-Host is read only when trustProxy is set.

nodes.label: tenant-domain:dns:sync (subdomain DNS reconciliation)
nodes.rationale: A job rather than a call inside the create endpoint, because a DNS write is slow and externally owned: in-request it would block on Cloudflare and a failure would leave a row that never resolves with nothing to retry it. A drifted record is MOVED, never joined by a second one (two A records read as an intermittent outage), and nothing is ever deleted. The worker holds SELECT only, so a compromised worker cannot alter the hostname->tenant mapping.

nodes.label: Dangling-DNS domain takeover residual risk (M1)
nodes.rationale: verify activates a domain from in-row fields with no outbound ownership proof, and the global-unique index is scoped to non-deleted rows, so tenant A can delete a mapping while leaving DNS pointed at the platform and tenant B re-registers and verifies the same hostname. Before untrusted self-service custom domains: keep activation operator-gated or wire real DNS-token proof.

nodes.label: authorizeInTransaction (identity-access chokepoint)
nodes.rationale: Default-deny ABAC inside withTenant, with RLS FORCE as defense in depth over the explicit tenant_id filter.

nodes.label: tenant-domain test suite (RLS proven under awcms_app)
nodes.rationale: A DB-gated integration test proves a direct SELECT returns zero rows without tenant context while the SECURITY DEFINER lookup still resolves an active domain and never exposes a secret column.
nodes.norm_label: tenant-domain test suite (rls proven under awcms_app)

nodes.label: theming module
nodes.rationale: The first website module implemented directly in the awcms base — the evidence for ADR-0034's decision that content/website modules may live in src/modules/ here, superseding the old no-content-website-modules restriction.

nodes.label: ADR-0034 (templates used directly; derived-application pathway removed)
nodes.norm_label: adr-0034 (templates used directly; derived-application pathway removed)

nodes.label: Trusted build-time code vs tenant-authored data
nodes.rationale: A tenant SELECTS a reviewed theme and CONFIGURES it by data only — no uploaded code, no arbitrary templates, no raw CSS/HTML/JS, and no database-stored executable template anywhere.
nodes.norm_label: trusted build-time code vs tenant-authored data

nodes.label: ThemeDescriptor + theme-registry.ts
nodes.rationale: Composed from reviewed in-repo base themes and bundled at build time; assertValidThemeDescriptor is its CSP/a11y gate. There is no derived-repo theme seam, so new themes live directly in this registry.

nodes.label: ThemeConfig (awcms_theming_config_versions, sql/033)
nodes.rationale: Token overrides, slot selections, media ids, section order and nav placement stored in the DB, schema-validated and bounded, RLS FORCE'd.

nodes.label: Validation by REJECTION, never sanitization
nodes.rationale: Rejecting rather than stripping sidesteps the incomplete-multi-character-sanitization class entirely; grammars are strict and linear (no ReDoS), font families come from a per-theme allow-list so no font value is ever tenant-authored.

nodes.label: serializeThemeTokensCss + /theming/{tenantCode}/tokens.css
nodes.rationale: Safe by construction (re-validates every value) and served as an EXTERNAL same-origin stylesheet, so style-src 'self' is never weakened by a per-request inline <style>.

nodes.label: Theme lifecycle: draft -> validate -> preview -> publish -> rollback/retire
nodes.rationale: Published versions are immutable (INSERT-only engine plus a BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE trigger); rollback and retire move only the active pointer, so history stays intact. All high-risk mutations are Idempotency-Keyed, ABAC-gated and audited.
nodes.norm_label: theme lifecycle: draft -> validate -> preview -> publish -> rollback/retire

nodes.label: Preview session (domain/preview-token.ts)
nodes.rationale: Short-lived, non-indexable, authorized: token stored as a hash, X-Robots-Tag noindex, private/no-store, and a distinct URL namespace from the public stylesheet so it cannot poison the public/CDN cache. Every read filters expires_at >= now(), so a stale session is inert without any purge job.

nodes.label: media_library dropped — theme-media.ts is a documented no-op
nodes.rationale: Asset-URL resolution returns an empty map so assets are omitted and the theme degrades safely, while stored asset ids remain valid DATA for when a media module lands.
nodes.norm_label: media_library dropped — theme-media.ts is a documented no-op

nodes.label: /admin/theming console
nodes.rationale: The draft editor is generated from the SELECTED descriptor (one control per declared token/slot/asset slot); reads reuse the same application functions the GET endpoint uses inside one withTenantOrThrow, every write goes to the guarded endpoints with a fresh Idempotency-Key except the read-only validate.

nodes.label: visitor_analytics module
nodes.rationale: type: system like reporting/logging — human visitor telemetry is platform observability every tenant shares the mechanism of, and its higher volume plus different retention/privacy needs are exactly why it is its own module.

nodes.label: Off by default (VISITOR_ANALYTICS_ENABLED)
nodes.rationale: A fresh install collects nothing until an operator opts in, and that software switch is never itself the lawful-basis/consent decision UU PDP requires — it only enables the mechanism.

nodes.label: domain/visitor-key.ts (tenant-bound salted HMAC identifiers)
nodes.rationale: Cookie, IP and user-agent are stored only as HMAC-SHA256 keyed by a deployment salt AND bound to the tenant id via a NUL domain separator: the salt gives cross-deployment rainbow-table resistance, the binding gives cross-tenant unlinkability, so two tenants' hash columns cannot be correlated at the storage layer. A real salt of >= 16 chars is enforced at env validation.

nodes.label: Raw-detail opt-in routed through evaluateFieldAccessInTransaction
nodes.rationale: The field decision goes through the ABAC evaluator, not a bare permission-set membership check, so a deny DSL policy on raw_detail.read is honored (deny-overrides-allow); the omission itself happens once, server-side, in analytics-response-shaping.ts.

nodes.label: domain/path-sanitizer.ts + domain/referrer.ts
nodes.rationale: Fail-safe: an unparseable path drops its whole query string; only a bare referrer hostname is kept, and even the two jsonb catch-alls hold derived values only.

nodes.label: awcms_visit_events (cross-tenant-safe composite FK)
nodes.rationale: (tenant_id, visitor_session_id) -> awcms_visitor_sessions (tenant_id, id), because a plain id FK would silently cross tenants; identity_id stays a plain nullable FK since the public ingest never populates it.

nodes.label: POST /api/v1/analytics/collect (public beacon)
nodes.rationale: Port adaptation: awcms-micro collected from middleware, this base leaves middleware untouched and exposes the collector as an additive opt-in beacon. IP/user-agent come from the request's own headers, never the body; it is fire-and-forget (always 202) and records public-area page views only, because an anonymous beacon cannot prove an admin/API request.

nodes.label: Per-IP rate-limit backstop on the beacon
nodes.rationale: An unauthenticated DB write must be bounded before any database work so a holder of a public tenantCode cannot flood rows or poison aggregates; the key is the client IP only, never the tenant, so a 429 reveals nothing about tenant existence.
nodes.norm_label: per-ip rate-limit backstop on the beacon

nodes.label: _shared/keyset-pagination.ts (full-precision text cursor)
nodes.rationale: Directories build the cursor from the row's own to_char(... US ...) microsecond text, never a floored JS Date.

nodes.label: application/retention-purge.ts
nodes.rationale: Log-like high-volume rows have no soft delete: the purge deletes aged events, clears session raw detail, deletes orphaned sessions and aged rollups.

nodes.label: LegalHoldGuardPort gate on the purge
nodes.rationale: An active hold skips the ENTIRE purge, not just the events DELETE as awcms-micro did, because steps 2-4 also destroy litigation-relevant data (IP/login snapshot, aggregates) — over-preserving under a hold is the safe default.

nodes.label: analytics:rollup / analytics:purge jobs
nodes.rationale: Both run on the shared job runner as the least-privilege awcms_worker role; pure PostgreSQL, safe offline/LAN, and the purge is meant to be dry-run first.

nodes.label: domain/geo-enrichment.ts (country-only)
nodes.rationale: Country only, from Cloudflare's CF-IPCountry and only when both geo and trust-Cloudflare flags are set; region/city/timezone are always null and it never makes an external network call.

nodes.label: /admin/analytics (server-rendered)
nodes.rationale: Port adaptation: awcms-micro's client-fetch SPA dashboard is rendered server-side here (the same SSR-read-then-render pattern admin/offices.astro uses) — no client script, no CSP surface.

nodes.label: workflow_approval module
nodes.rationale: Evolved from a linear engine into a managed, versioned, graph-based enterprise minimum while keeping the base guardrail: no domain-specific business terms/actions, no external BPMN engine, and no runtime code execution in conditions/actions.

nodes.label: domain/workflow-graph.ts (closed node-type set)
nodes.rationale: approval / condition / parallel / join / notify / end — a small closed set, never a scripting or expression engine; a condition is EITHER a bounded comparison over a declared fact OR a statically-registered resolver, never both and never neither.

nodes.label: validateWorkflowGraph
nodes.rationale: Structurally validates node references, quorum bounds and parallel/join branch-set matching and rejects cycles by DFS — run on every definition write and again at publish, as defense in depth.

nodes.label: domain/workflow-quorum.ts
nodes.rationale: A single reject always completes the node as rejected regardless of the quorum rule — a deliberate, documented conservative default.

nodes.label: awcms_workflow_task_assignments
nodes.rationale: Assignment rows are never deleted, only marked reassigned — the history is append-only.

nodes.label: awcms_workflow_join_arrivals
nodes.rationale: Append-only fan-in bookkeeping, idempotent by unique constraint; it assumes one level of nesting, which is why nested parallel/join is unsupported.

nodes.label: WorkflowConditionResolver / WorkflowActionHandler static registry
nodes.rationale: A static, reviewed-source-code registry mirroring domain-event-runtime's consumer registry; it ships one reference resolver and one reference action handler to prove the mechanism end-to-end without inventing business logic — an action NODE TYPE that would call the handler does not exist yet.

nodes.label: Definition version pinning
nodes.rationale: An immutable FK plus a denormalized version pin every instance to the exact definition row active when it started; because published/active/retired rows are never edited in place, every later read re-fetches the identical graph regardless of newer versions.

nodes.label: Task-decision serialisation (FOR UPDATE OF t)
nodes.rationale: Quorum is never evaluated on a snapshot that cannot see a sibling's in-flight decision; the loser blocks and re-reads the winner's committed row, which is what makes the status check a correct 409 gate. Chosen over an advisory lock because the lock sits on the very row whose status is the invariant and also interlocks with cancel/reassign/force/escalation. OF t is deliberate — a bare FOR UPDATE would serialise every instance sharing the definition.

nodes.label: One live seat per person per task (GHSA-9qwq-cmr5-6wfc)
nodes.rationale: A partial unique index is the durable invariant, both INSERT paths are ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, and quorum counts DISTINCT people, never rows — otherwise a user who was both assignee and escalation target held two seats and could satisfy a 2-person quorum alone. Reassigning to someone who already decided is refused rather than granting a second vote.
nodes.norm_label: one live seat per person per task (ghsa-9qwq-cmr5-6wfc)

nodes.label: Terminal-status guard on the end-node UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Conditioned on status = 'pending' and rolled back if it matches nothing, so an in-flight decision can never resurrect a cancelled instance.
nodes.norm_label: terminal-status guard on the end-node update

nodes.label: domain/workflow-delegation.ts
nodes.rationale: A delegation only lets the delegate act using the delegator's OWN standing — never a permission grant and never wider than its declared workflowKey/resourceType/window; self-approval denial still compares the ACTING user, so a delegate cannot approve a request the delegator filed.

nodes.label: application/workflow-escalation.ts + escalations dispatch job
nodes.rationale: The UPDATE is conditioned on the escalation_step read this pass, so a lost race affects zero rows and is silently skipped rather than double-escalating; the target INSERT is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING because adding a seat someone already holds would hand them a second quorum vote.

nodes.label: application/workflow-recovery.ts (reassign/cancel/force-decision)
nodes.rationale: Each permission-gated, reason-required, Idempotency-Keyed and audited; it never overwrites or deletes a prior decision/task/assignment row — always a new row or a guarded status transition.

nodes.label: application/workflow-inbox-directory.ts (consolidated inbox)
nodes.rationale: Keyset pagination on (created_at, id), filters, and safe parameterized ILIKE search with escaped wildcards — never string concatenation. Instance detail reuses decisions + audit events rather than adding a history table.

nodes.label: Self-approval guard (evaluateAccess, access-control.ts)
nodes.rationale: Reused unchanged, not a new mechanism: the route looks up the instance's requester BEFORE the guard so the comparison has the right value.

nodes.label: Generic SoD layer (Issue #181, ADR-0031)
nodes.rationale: Complementary, not a duplicate: the workflow guard is a same-instance creator-not-approver check, while SoD enforces registered conflicting-permission pairs fail-closed at the chokepoint. A future SoD rule targeting a workflow permission would first need the approve route migrated onto authorizeInTransaction — no active gap today because the base ships no SoD rules.

nodes.label: force-decision self-approval bypass (High, PR #778)
nodes.rationale: The route authorized without populating requestedByTenantUserId and the self-approval deny check was hardwired to the approve action, so a caller holding force_decide could force-approve their own request and bypass quorum entirely; fixed by looking up the instance before the guard and extending the deny check to force_decide.

nodes.label: Missing audit/Idempotency-Key findings (PR #778)
nodes.rationale: publish, retire, definitions DELETE and delegation create/revoke were high-risk mutations that recorded no audit event, and three of them enforced no Idempotency-Key; separately the seeded workflow.delegation.revoke permission was dead because the route gated on read and relied on the ownership check alone.

nodes.label: awcms_idempotency_keys (generic store, migration 012)
nodes.rationale: Same key + same request hash replays the stored response; same key + different hash is a 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

nodes.label: Workflow metrics (metrics-port.ts)
nodes.rationale: All unlabeled or labeled with a fixed code-defined enum only — never a tenant or resource id; per-workflow breakdowns would need a bounded-cardinality follow-up, not unbounded labels.

nodes.label: /admin/approvals inbox
nodes.rationale: The UI is never the enforcement point, only a strictly-more-restrictive convenience layer. Cancel lives on the instance panel, not the task row, because it ends the whole instance and every pending task — offering it beside one task would misrepresent its blast radius.

nodes.label: No definition/graph editor, deliberately
nodes.rationale: A raw-JSON textarea that accepts a malformed graph until publish rejects it is a worse affordance than none, so the six definition.* permissions are claimed by no screen and a contract test asserts they stay off the page — keeping the split a decision rather than a gap.

nodes.label: Least-privilege worker grant verified per write path
nodes.rationale: The escalation job only reads instances and writes tasks, so awcms_worker gets SELECT-only on instances — verified per write path rather than copied from mini, avoiding the SELECT, UPDATE over-grant an earlier mini migration shipped.
nodes.norm_label: least-privilege worker grant verified per write path

nodes.label: Frozen awcms-astro consumer contract
nodes.rationale: Regenerating is a DELIBERATE act meaning the contract changed and the consumer must change with it; the check is a subset assertion, so additive changes (a new optional field, a new enum value) need no regeneration. The file exists to stop awcms-astro's build breaking silently.

nodes.label: accessListMachineCredentials
nodes.rationale: Returns derived active/expired/revoked status plus lastUsedAt so a leak can be traced without any secret material leaving the server.

nodes.label: accessIssueMachineCredential
nodes.rationale: Returns the plaintext token exactly once and is deliberately NOT idempotency-keyed, because replaying the response would mean persisting the token. The credential AUTHENTICATES only — every request still passes module-enabled, RBAC, ABAC and SoD.

nodes.label: MachineCredential schema
nodes.rationale: Never carries the token or its hash: tracing a leak needs to know which credential is alive and whether anything uses it, and none of that requires secret material. allowedPermissionKeys NARROWS by intersection with the service account's roles and can never widen them; lastUsedAt refreshes at most hourly so an idle credential is visible without a write per request.

nodes.label: IssueMachineCredentialRequest schema
nodes.rationale: An empty allowedPermissionKeys list means 'can do nothing', never 'unrestricted'; read is rejected in allowedWriteActions rather than accepted as a no-op, and allowedIpCidrs is rejected for a read-only credential because accepting it would describe a binding that is not enforced. There is no perpetual credential.

nodes.label: Two credential classes, two permissions (ADR-0092 write class)
nodes.rationale: Naming write actions switches the guard to a SEPARATE machine_credentials_write.create key, so opening the write class does not hand write-minting authority to every role that already holds create. The write class is narrower everywhere else: code-ceiling actions only, at least one CIDR, at most 30 days, and an unknown caller IP is refused rather than exempted.
nodes.norm_label: two credential classes, two permissions (adr-0092 write class)

nodes.label: introspectAuthSession (GET /api/v1/auth/session)
nodes.rationale: For awcms-astro's BFF, which holds the session token server-side; a browser never calls it. Anti-oracle: missing bearer, unknown/expired/revoked session, deactivated identity and a machine credential presented here all produce the SAME 401, rate-limited per source with private, no-store on every path.

nodes.label: SessionIntrospection schema
nodes.rationale: Safe claims only — never a token, token hash, password state, MFA secret/recovery code, or raw email/phone identifier; scopes are the same effective-dated business-scope evaluation the authorization layer uses.

nodes.label: The default response is BlogPostSummary, not BlogPost
nodes.rationale: This document used to say otherwise and a client that believed it built an entire static site with every article body empty — nothing failed, because a missing field reads as undefined. A caller needing the body asks for view=full.
nodes.norm_label: the default response is blogpostsummary, not blogpost

nodes.label: Cursor traversal requires order=created_at
nodes.rationale: updated_at DESC is right for an admin table and unsound as a keyset key, because editing a post moves it and a row can cross a page boundary and be skipped or repeated; a cursor without order=created_at is refused with 400 rather than quietly honoured, and the ordering is demanded rather than silently substituted.

nodes.label: blogCreatePost (POST /api/v1/blog/posts)
nodes.rationale: Not idempotency-keyed: a retry duplicating a create is caught by the (tenant_id, locale, slug) partial unique index.

nodes.label: mediaResolveObjects (GET /api/v1/media/objects)
nodes.rationale: Batch rather than one-per-id because a build feed resolves every image on a page at once and the query is already a single id = ANY(...). Unknown, cross-tenant, unverified and deleted ids all land in ONE unresolved bucket so the response is not an oracle, while a malformed uuid is a 400 — 'you sent junk' and 'that object is not referenceable' are different facts.

nodes.label: mediaPublicOrigin (GET /api/v1/media/public-origin)
nodes.rationale: A build client's CSP must name the media host in img-src BEFORE fetching any object — an image resolved correctly still renders as nothing when the policy blocks its host; the alternative is two hand-copied values that agree until one is edited. Both origin and baseUrl are reported because neither choice is this API's to make, and a deployment serving no public media answers 200 with configured:false so a build can omit the entry instead of failing.
